grounded_facts: An annual formal dinner event hosted by the Sarah Siddons Society to honor distinguished achievements in theater, culminating in the presentation of the Sarah Siddons Award.
memories.memory_text: I was at the Sarah Siddons Society's annual banquet, where they honor distinguished achievements in theater with the Sarah Siddons Award.

grounded_facts: Addison deWitt narrates an introduction of Karen Richards, commenting on her connection to the theater through marriage.
memories.memory_text: I heard Addison deWitt introduce Karen Richards, saying she was connected to the theater only by marriage, not by background or breeding.

grounded_facts: Addison deWitt identifies Max Fabian as a theatrical producer driven by financial risk rather than art.
memories.memory_text: I listened as Addison deWitt described Max Fabian as a producer focused on financial risk, someone out to make a buck rather than driven by art.

grounded_facts: Addison deWitt presents Margo Channing as a legendary theater star whose role was given to Eve Harrington.
memories.memory_text: I heard Addison deWitt present me as a legendary theater star, and then say that the role Eve Harrington was being honored for was originally meant for me.

grounded_facts: It is disclosed that the role for which Eve Harrington won the award was originally meant for Margo Channing.
memories.memory_text: I was told that the part for which Eve Harrington received the Sarah Siddons Award was originally meant for me.

grounded_facts: The aged actor delivers a ceremonial speech extolling Eve Harrington's youth, humility, and devotion to theater.
memories.memory_text: I watched the aged actor deliver his speech, praising Eve Harrington's youth, humility, and devotion to the theater, and I heard him present her with the Sarah Siddons Award for distinguished achievement.

grounded_facts: Eve Harrington is formally presented with the Sarah Siddons Award for Distinguished Achievement in a public ceremony, with the action pausing at the moment of award transfer as sound and motion stop.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve Harrington formally receive the Sarah Siddons Award in the public ceremony, and I remember the moment when she moved toward the aged actor, the applause still rising, and everything seemed to pause as the award was about to be placed in her hands.

grounded_facts: The moment when Margo Channing exits the theater after performing in 'Aged in Wood,' with theater lights dimming and the audience dispersing.
memories.memory_text: I remember exiting the theater after performing in 'Aged in Wood,' the lights dimming behind me and the audience beginning to disperse.

grounded_facts: Karen decides to bring Eve to meet Margo Channing after learning about her devotion as a fan.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Karen decided to bring Eve to meet me after hearing about her devotion as a fan.

grounded_facts: When asked, Eve introduces herself by name for the first time.
memories.memory_text: I was asked my name, so I introduced myself as Eve Harrington for the first time.

grounded_facts: Eve, accompanied by Karen, arrives at Margo's dressing room door, waiting briefly before entering as Margo speaks from inside.
An informal moment in Margo's dressing room where she speaks loudly from within, engaging someone inside while Karen and Eve arrive outside.
memories.memory_text: I was inside my dressing room, speaking loudly and laughing, when I sensed someone arriving at the door—Karen and Eve, though I didn’t acknowledge them right away.

grounded_facts: Margo delivers a loud, humorous line from inside the dressing room, referencing a hypothetical Southern victory in the Civil War.
memories.memory_text: I called out loudly from inside the dressing room, joking that if the South had won the war, someone could write the same plays about the North instead.

grounded_facts: Karen reveals that Eve Harrington, a devoted fan, is waiting outside Margo's dressing room and insists Margo see her.
Karen insists that Margo meet Eve, emphasizing Eve's devotion and emotional investment.
memories.memory_text: I remember Karen telling me that Eve Harrington, a devoted fan, was waiting outside my dressing room and insisting I see her, saying she worshipped me and had been coming to every performance.

grounded_facts: A private gathering in Margo's dressing room after a performance, involving close associates and a visiting fan.
memories.memory_text: I was in my dressing room after the show, just me and my close friends, when Karen brought Eve in and we all shared a quiet moment together.

grounded_facts: Margo uses quiet menace to send Birdie back to the bathroom to avoid disruption during Eve's introduction.
memories.memory_text: I used a quiet, firm tone to tell Birdie she should go back to the bathroom, making it clear she needed to leave us alone during Eve's introduction.

grounded_facts: Eve tells Margo she has attended every performance and that seeing her is the only meaningful activity in her life.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Eve that she's attended every one of my performances and that seeing me is the only meaningful thing in her life.

grounded_facts: Eve recounts her isolated upbringing in Wisconsin and the death of her husband Eddie in the war, explaining how attending Margo's performance of 'Remembrance' in San Francisco became a turning point, forging her deep emotional attachment to Margo.
memories.memory_text: I listened as Eve told me about growing up isolated in Wisconsin, losing her husband Eddie in the war, and how coming to see my performance in 'Remembrance' in San Francisco became a turning point for her, the moment she says everything changed and her deep connection to me began.

grounded_facts: After mocking Eve's story, Birdie sincerely apologizes, acknowledging her bluntness and showing unexpected respect.
memories.memory_text: I saw Birdie mock Eve's story and then apologize sincerely, admitting her bluntness in that moment.

grounded_facts: Bill Sampson enters Margo's dressing room unannounced, disrupting the gathering with his energetic and chaotic presence, revealing he is about to leave for a film shoot.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill bursting into my dressing room with that loud, chaotic energy of his, suitcase in hand, cutting right through the moment I was having—telling me he was about to leave for a film shoot, calling me his 'wonderful junk yard' like it was some kind of endearment.

grounded_facts: Bill briefly acknowledges Eve only after being reminded by Karen, showing little interest or respect.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill barely acknowledge Eve, just asking her name as if he hadn't already met her, and only after Karen reminded him did he even pretend to remember—showing no real interest or respect.

grounded_facts: Margo impulsively decides to delay her departure with Bill to spend time alone with Eve after the others leave.
Margo insists Eve stay after others leave, signaling a shift from skepticism to personal investment in their connection.
memories.memory_text: I impulsively decided to delay leaving with Bill and asked Eve to stay behind so we could talk alone after everyone else left.

grounded_facts: Karen tells Eve she hopes to see her again not just as a fan, but as a friend, extending personal warmth.
memories.memory_text: I heard Karen tell Eve that she hoped to see her again not just as a fan, but as a friend, and it struck me how warmly she spoke to her.

grounded_facts: Eve tells Karen she will never forget the night or her role in making it possible, emphasizing emotional significance.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve tell Karen she would never forget that night or her part in making it possible, and I noticed how deeply she meant it.

grounded_facts: Bill explains his philosophical view of theater, justifying his decision to go to Hollywood as an expansion of theatrical art beyond traditional boundaries.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill sit up and passionately explain that theater isn't just in New York or London—it's anywhere there's magic and an audience, including Hollywood, rodeos, and even Donald Duck.

grounded_facts: Eve persistently questions Bill's motivation for going to Hollywood, implying disapproval or concern.
memories.memory_text: I heard Eve questioning Bill about why he had to go to Hollywood, and she told him he shouldn't stay there, which made me realize she was really doubtful about his decision.

grounded_facts: Margo cannot find her second earring while preparing to leave.
memories.memory_text: I couldn't find my other earring while I was getting ready to leave, and I remember saying it must be the latest thing—just one earring—if it wasn't already.

grounded_facts: Margo finds and then throws away a letter she has been carrying, prompted by Bill's comment.
memories.memory_text: I found the letter I'd been holding and threw it away, right after Bill made his remark.

grounded_facts: Bill tells Margo to throw away a letter she's been carrying, calling it dreary and boring.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Bill to throw away that dreary letter I'd been carrying because it bored him.

grounded_facts: Bill embraces Birdie and kisses her cheek before leaving; she returns the kiss.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill embrace Birdie and kiss her cheek before leaving, and she kissed him back.

grounded_facts: Birdie tells Bill to 'kill the people' as a way of wishing him success at the event.
memories.memory_text: I heard Birdie tell Bill to 'kill the people' as he was heading out.

grounded_facts: Margo, Eve, Bill, and Birdie gather in Margo's dressing room as she finishes getting ready to attend a public event.
memories.memory_text: I remember putting on one earring in the bathroom and calling out that I couldn't find the other, then Birdie followed me out as I joined Eve, Bill, and her in my dressing room before we headed out together.

grounded_facts: Margo and Eve leave the dressing room ahead of Bill, marking the end of preparation and transition to the awards event.
memories.memory_text: I left the dressing room with Eve ahead of Bill, ready to head to the awards ceremony.

grounded_facts: A logistical and emotional moment at LaGuardia Field where Margo, Bill, and Eve prepare for Bill's flight departure.
memories.memory_text: I was at LaGuardia with Bill, my arm through his, feeling the weight of our last moments together before he had to leave, while Eve stood nearby.

grounded_facts: Eve proposes to take care of the check-in procedures so Margo and Bill can spend their last moments together before departure.
Eve verbally proposes to manage the check-in so Margo and Bill can have private time before Bill's departure.
memories.memory_text: I remember Eve offering to handle the check-in so Bill and I could have some private time before his flight, saying she could meet us at the gate with the ticket.

grounded_facts: Bill gives the airplane ticket to Eve, authorizing her to complete the check-in process.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill give the airplane ticket to Eve, letting her take over the check-in.

grounded_facts: Margo smiles gratefully at Eve after she accepts the task of handling check-in.
memories.memory_text: I smiled gratefully at Eve when she took on the task of handling check-in, because it meant I could have a moment with Bill.

grounded_facts: Margo cautions Bill not to become infatuated with Eve, whom she sees as a naive young woman vulnerable in their world.
memories.memory_text: I warned Bill not to get infatuated with some naive girl like Eve, telling him not to get stuck on a glamour puss—she doesn't understand our world and could be dangerous in it.

grounded_facts: Margo directly asks Bill if she is going to lose him, revealing her emotional dependence and fear of abandonment.
memories.memory_text: I asked Bill, 'Am I going to lose you, Bill? Am I?' because I couldn't hold back my fear of him leaving me, and his response—'How childish are you going to get before you quit it?'—only deepened my insecurity.

grounded_facts: Bill stops kissing Margo upon noticing Eve standing near them with his ticket.
memories.memory_text: I was about to be kissed by Bill when he suddenly stopped, and I noticed Eve standing right there with his ticket.

grounded_facts: Eve hands Bill his ticket, indicating readiness to proceed toward the gate.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve hand Bill his ticket, and then they started moving toward the gate together.

grounded_facts: A moment at LaGuardia airport where Bill and Margo are preparing to leave, interrupted by Eve's arrival with the ticket.
memories.memory_text: I was there with Bill at LaGuardia, about to leave, when Eve suddenly showed up with his ticket and interrupted us—I saw her standing there, handing it to him, and then we all started toward the gate.

grounded_facts: Bill asks Eve to look after Margo in his absence, framing her as someone who needs companionship.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Bill to keep an eye on Margo and not let her get lonely, as if she were a loose lamb in a jungle.

grounded_facts: Bill boards the plane after saying goodbye to Margo and Eve, marking his physical departure from the scene.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill pause on his way to the plane, then wave and climb aboard before the door closed and the departure began—I watched him go, knowing he was really leaving.

grounded_facts: A farewell gathering at the boarding gate as Bill departs on a flight.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill holding me close and us kissing before he left—I held on tightly, but he pulled away and started toward the plane. I turned away, and Eve linked her arm through mine. He paused, then waved and boarded the plane while I stood there with Eve, and we eventually walked off together as she moved her arm to comfort me.

grounded_facts: After Bill leaves, Eve shifts from linking arms to placing her arm comfortingly around Margo as they walk.
memories.memory_text: After Bill left, I felt Eve shift her arm from linking with mine to placing it comfortingly around me as we walked away.

grounded_facts: Addison offers Margo a drink; she declines absently, indicating preoccupation with her thoughts about Eve.
memories.memory_text: I was lost in thought about Eve, barely noticing when Addison offered me a drink—I shook my head without really seeing him, my mind still tangled in memories of her.

grounded_facts: Eve brings letters for Margo to sign and exchanges them for the script Margo returns.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting by the fire with my script when Eve brought over a stack of letters for me to sign, and I handed her the script in exchange.

grounded_facts: Eve intercepts the phone call and skillfully rejects the caller, demonstrating control over access to Margo.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve get to the phone before Birdie and politely turn the caller away, handling things as if she were in charge.

grounded_facts: Birdie glares at Eve after she intercepts the phone call, showing resentment toward Eve's growing influence.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Birdie glaring at Eve and then at me, clearly upset about how Eve stepped in and took control.

grounded_facts: Birdie slams the door as she leaves after being overridden by Eve in answering the phone.
memories.memory_text: I saw Birdie slam the door as she left after Eve took over answering the phone.

grounded_facts: Margo decides not to take another curtain call, signaling a shift in her relationship with audience validation.
Post-performance audience acknowledgment where Margo receives repeated applause.
memories.memory_text: I decided not to take another curtain call after the applause, realizing it no longer meant what it used to—I just wanted to get off the stage.

grounded_facts: Eve tells Margo she could watch her perform the final scene a thousand times and cry each time.
Eve tells Margo she is profoundly moved by her performance, revealing emotional investment and reverence.
memories.memory_text: I remember Eve telling me she could watch my final scene a thousand times and still cry, and how deeply moved she said she was by my performance.

grounded_facts: Margo responds to Eve's praise with self-deprecating humor about performing a thousand times.
memories.memory_text: I joked with Eve that if I ever performed that scene a thousand times, I’d probably be doing it from a padded room.

grounded_facts: Margo and Eve transition from the stage area to Margo's dressing room, initiating a private post-show interaction.
memories.memory_text: I walked off the stage with Eve, leaving the applause behind, and we began moving toward my dressing room to talk privately.

grounded_facts: Eve helps Margo unhook her gown, indicating intimacy and service.
Margo allows Eve to help her unhook her gown as they enter the dressing room.
memories.memory_text: I let Eve help me unhook my gown when we got to the dressing room, and I could feel her admiration as she stood close behind me.

grounded_facts: Eve expresses disapproval of how the cast has altered the production in the director's absence.
Eve points out deviations in staging since the director's absence, showing attention to detail and alignment with Margo's standards.
memories.memory_text: I remember Eve telling me how the cast has been changing everything in the production since the director left, and she pointed out that it's been disgraceful how they alter things, showing she really pays attention to the details I care about.

grounded_facts: Eve informs Margo that Roger Ferraday has been moving closer during her second-act scene.
Eve informs Margo about a specific deviation in Roger Ferraday's stage positioning during her scene with her father.
memories.memory_text: Eve informed me that Roger Ferraday has been moving closer each night during my second-act scene with my father, and I learned he’s supposed to stay upstage at the arch but keeps encroaching on my space.

grounded_facts: Margo jokingly threatens to spit in Roger Ferraday's eye if he continues moving closer during the scene.
Margo jokes that she will spit in Roger Ferraday's eye if he comes too close.
memories.memory_text: I joked that when Roger gets too close during the scene, I’ll spit in his eye—it was my way of making it clear I won’t tolerate him invading my space on stage.

grounded_facts: Eve takes initiative to return Margo's costume to the wardrobe mistress, overstepping her role.
memories.memory_text: I told Eve not to bother returning my costume because Mrs. Brown would come for it, but she said 'No trouble at all' and took it anyway—I saw her go out with it, and I knew that wasn't how things were done back there.

grounded_facts: Birdie indirectly alerts Margo that Eve is violating backstage norms by handling costume duties, implying potential trouble.
memories.memory_text: I heard Birdie say that wardrobe women are the touchiest thing in show business next to a tenor, and I realized something was off about Eve handling costume duties.

grounded_facts: Margo understands from Birdie's comment that Eve is encroaching on the duties of the unionized wardrobe mistress, which could cause conflict.
memories.memory_text: I thought about how the wardrobe staff are unionized, and I wasn't sure if Eve stepping in was allowed, so I got worried and rushed out after her.

grounded_facts: A private moment in Margo's dressing room after her stage performance, involving informal interaction with Birdie and Eve.
memories.memory_text: After my performance, I was in my dressing room, taking off my wig and getting into my robe while Eve sat on the chaise near my costume, and I remember saying to her, 'Just because you can't even work a zipper. It was very thoughtful, Eve, and I appreciate it—' before things took a turn.

grounded_facts: Eve holds Margo's dress against her body and mimics Margo's performance gestures in front of mirrors, indicating identification with or aspiration to Margo's role.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve holding my dress against her body and mimicking my performance gestures in front of the mirrors, and I smiled, recognizing how much she wants to be me.

grounded_facts: Margo stops Eve from continuing to wear or handle her dress by instructing that wardrobe should be handled by Mrs. Brown.
Margo quietly but firmly directs Eve to stop handling her costume, signaling disapproval and boundary-setting.
memories.memory_text: I quietly told Eve that we'd better let Mrs. Brown handle the wardrobe, making it clear she shouldn't be touching my costume anymore.

grounded_facts: Bill insists that Margo verbally express her love or sing it, refusing to let her end the call without affirmation.
memories.memory_text: I tried to end the call, but Bill insisted I say or sing that I love him before hanging up, refusing to let me off the phone.

grounded_facts: Margo becomes aware that she did not remember Bill's birthday and that the call was either misattributed or pre-arranged without her current recollection.
memories.memory_text: I realized I hadn't remembered Bill's birthday at all, and that someone else must have arranged the call, because I know damn well it wasn't me.

grounded_facts: Bill receives a phone call from Margo at exactly midnight, California time, which he believes was initiated by her to wish him a happy birthday.
memories.memory_text: I was awakened for a call I supposedly placed to Bill at midnight, California time, and I went along with it, wishing him a happy birthday even though I hadn't planned to call.

grounded_facts: The occasion of Bill's birthday, marked by a midnight phone call and emotional expectations around remembrance and celebration.
memories.memory_text: The call at midnight was meant to mark Bill's birthday, a moment he expected me to honor with celebration and affection, even though I had no intention of doing so.

grounded_facts: Bill mentions that Eve has been writing to him weekly and organizing his return party, indicating her increasing presence in his life during his absence.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Eve has been writing to Bill every week and organizing his return party, and that he even sent her a list of people to invite.

grounded_facts: When Bill asks about Eve, Margo responds with minimal engagement and deflects by saying she will 'check with Eve,' implying Eve now manages their shared social arrangements.
memories.memory_text: When Bill asked how Eve was, I said she was okay and then I told him I'd check with Eve about the plans, because she's the one handling everything now.

grounded_facts: Margo probes Birdie about her opinion of Eve, expressing subtle doubts about Eve's true intentions and level of devotion.
Margo directly asks Birdie if she likes Eve, seeking honest feedback.
memories.memory_text: I asked Birdie directly if she liked Eve because I wanted an honest answer, and I pressed her when she hesitated, even though I started by acknowledging Eve's loyalty and efficiency.

grounded_facts: Birdie suggests that Eve observes Margo with detached, analytical intensity, like studying a character in a play or blueprint.
Birdie tells Margo that Eve watches her like a character in a book or blueprint, implying surveillance.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Birdie that Eve watches me like she's studying a character in a play or a set of blueprints, observing how I walk, talk, think, eat, and sleep, which made me wonder about her true intentions.

grounded_facts: Eve admits she forgot to inform Margo about arranging a birthday message to Bill, but took initiative to send a telegram herself.
Eve reveals she sent a birthday telegram to Bill on Margo's behalf without informing her.
memories.memory_text: I was told Eve sent a birthday telegram to Bill on my behalf and forgot to inform me about it first.

grounded_facts: After Eve's revelation, Margo silently reflects, showing signs of growing distrust toward Eve's expanding role in her life.
memories.memory_text: After Eve left, I found myself staring at the door, silently turning over what she'd done, feeling a quiet unease grow inside me.

grounded_facts: A domestic morning scene where Margo receives breakfast and engages in conversations with Birdie and Eve.
memories.memory_text: I was in bed that morning, sipping orange juice while Birdie brought me breakfast, and later Eve came in with her portfolio before leaving again, and I just sat there afterward, staring at my drink.

grounded_facts: Margo silently toasts Karen by raising her glass, creating a moment of mutual recognition.
memories.memory_text: I raised my glass in a silent toast to Karen, and I could feel a moment of understanding pass between us.

grounded_facts: Karen reflects on her past encounters with Eve, noting they did not speak meaningfully until a later party.
memories.memory_text: I remember Karen telling me that she had seen Eve many times after their first meeting, but they never really spoke again until the party I gave for Bill when he came back from Hollywood.

grounded_facts: Karen reassures Eve that she is not a charity case and acknowledges her significant contributions to Margo's well-being.
memories.memory_text: I heard Karen tell Eve she wasn't a charity case and that she'd done a lot for me, which made me feel appreciated even from a distance.

grounded_facts: Eve expresses her desire to become Margo's new understudy, citing her deep knowledge of the role and staging, and asks Karen to speak to Mr. Fabian about it.
memories.memory_text: I overheard Eve expressing her desire to become my understudy, saying she knew the role well, and asking Karen to speak to Mr. Fabian about it.

grounded_facts: Eve hesitantly asks Karen to speak to Mr. Fabian about appointing her as Margo's understudy.
memories.memory_text: I recall Eve hesitantly asking Karen to talk to Mr. Fabian about appointing her as my understudy, her voice careful and polite.

grounded_facts: Eve hugs Karen in gratitude after securing her promise to advocate for the understudy position.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve hug Karen in gratitude after Karen agreed to advocate for her to become my understudy, then leave quickly.

grounded_facts: An ongoing party at Margo's home late at night, subdued in tone, with guests downstairs while private conversations occur in the bedroom.
memories.memory_text: I remember the party at my place that night was still going on downstairs, quiet but lingering, while Karen and Eve had their talk in my bedroom.

grounded_facts: Eve speaks passionately about the value of applause and audience love, revealing her deep emotional investment in theatrical recognition.
memories.memory_text: I remember Eve speaking so passionately about applause, saying it was like waves of love from the audience, and I could tell how much she craved that recognition.

grounded_facts: A late-night informal assembly of theater people on the stairs after a party, marked by intellectual banter, emotional tension, and eventual conflict.
memories.memory_text: I was drinking too much that night, and I remember snapping at Eve to stop acting like I was royalty, mocking her as a busy little bee, and later telling Bill to take over hosting—I just wanted out of that tense, buzzing group.

grounded_facts: Margo sarcastically implies Eve would willingly perform intimate acts to serve her, rejecting Eve's offer with contempt.
memories.memory_text: I sarcastically asked Eve if she'd take my clothes off and tuck me in, just to show how insincere her eagerness to serve was—I wouldn't like that at all.

grounded_facts: Intoxicated and defensive, Margo mocks Eve's deference and abruptly ends the evening by going to bed, assigning Bill the role of host.
memories.memory_text: I was drinking too much and feeling defensive, so I told everyone I was going to bed and told Bill to host instead—I needed to get out of there.

grounded_facts: A party held to welcome Bill back and celebrate his birthday at the Sarah Siddons Society dining hall.
memories.memory_text: I remember the party held to welcome Bill back and celebrate his birthday at the Sarah Siddons Society dining hall — it was supposed to be a celebration, but the setting itself felt charged with tension.

grounded_facts: Margo reflects on the party as a historical disaster, expressing her negative anticipation and judgment.
memories.memory_text: Even before the party started, I could smell disaster in the air — I knew it would go down in history like the Chicago Fire or the Massacre of the Huguenots; I already judged it a catastrophe in my mind.

grounded_facts: An upcoming social gathering hosted by Margo, for which she is preparing.
memories.memory_text: I was getting ready for a party I was hosting, though I already had a bad feeling about how the night would go.

grounded_facts: Margo finishes dressing and puts on jewelry before the party, expressing premonition about the evening.
memories.memory_text: I knew it, I sensed it even as I finished dressing for that blasted party...

grounded_facts: Birdie relays a message from the bartender regarding a mix-up with the gin order.
memories.memory_text: I was told there's a message from the bartender asking if I know we ordered domestic gin by mistake.

grounded_facts: Margo makes a sarcastic remark implying regret over inviting her guests.
memories.memory_text: I said the only thing I ordered by mistake is the guests, making a sarcastic remark about regretting inviting them.

grounded_facts: Margo expresses concern about Bill being late, only to learn from Birdie that he has already arrived twenty minutes ago.
memories.memory_text: I asked where Bill was because I thought he was late, but Birdie told me he'd already been there for twenty minutes, and I found it odd that he hadn't come to see me.

grounded_facts: Birdie assists Margo by zipping the back of her dress, completing her outfit.
memories.memory_text: I asked Birdie to zip the back of my dress, and she did—then I met her glance and walked out, ready for the evening.

grounded_facts: Margo increases her pace while descending the stairs, indicating urgency or anxiety.
memories.memory_text: I increased my pace going down the stairs, feeling the urgency in my steps.

grounded_facts: Margo deliberately reaches the landing and begins moving toward the living room where Bill and Eve are conversing.
memories.memory_text: I deliberately made my way to the landing and started moving toward the living room where Bill and Eve were talking.

grounded_facts: An informal moment of shared laughter and storytelling between Bill and Eve in the living room, interrupted by Margo's arrival.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill telling a story while Eve sat there laughing and hanging on his words, clearly enjoying the moment together.

grounded_facts: Upon seeing Margo approach, Eve stops laughing, ends her engagement with Bill's story, and stands up.
Margo's deliberate arrival and approach cause Eve to stop laughing and stand up, and Bill to turn around, ending the intimacy of the moment.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Eve stop laughing and stand up as I approached, and Bill turned to face me, ending their little intimate scene.

grounded_facts: Margo confronts Bill about his extended conversation with Eve, interpreting it as a sign of romantic interest and expressing jealousy masked as criticism of Eve's 'qualities'.
Margo implies that Bill is overly impressed by Eve's youth and supposed virtues, using sarcasm to express her insecurity.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Bill about how long he was talking with Eve, and I sarcastically pointed out her so-called 'qualities'—her loyalty, efficiency, devotion, warmth, affection, and how young she is—because I could tell he was impressed by her youth, and it made me jealous.

grounded_facts: Bill rebukes Margo for judging Eve harshly, framing her behavior as innocent admiration and accusing Margo of insecurity.
memories.memory_text: Bill rebuked me, telling me I was judging Eve too harshly and that her behavior was just innocent admiration; he accused me of being insecure and even called it a paranoid insecurity I should be ashamed of.

grounded_facts: When offered a drink by Bill, Eve looks to Margo for approval, acknowledging her as the authority figure.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Eve looking to me for approval when Bill offered her a drink, as if I had the final say in what she could do.

grounded_facts: After downing her drink, Margo delivers a dramatic line signaling the beginning of a turbulent evening, marking a shift in tone.
memories.memory_text: I downed my drink and told everyone to fasten their seat belts—it was going to be a bumpy night.

grounded_facts: A gathering at Margo's home on a snowy night, hosted in anticipation of a larger celebration, where personal tensions and power dynamics surface among guests from the theater world.
memories.memory_text: I remember that snowy night at my place, hosting everyone before the big celebration, when tensions started rising—Bill went to get Eve a drink, someone mentioned a five-and-ten-cent store, and I introduced Eve to an old friend, all while feeling the power shifting around me.

grounded_facts: Addison tells Margo not to worry about Eve, implying he now has responsibility for her, undermining Margo's authority.
memories.memory_text: Addison told me not to worry about my little charge, said Eve was in safe hands, and I could see he meant to take control of the situation.

grounded_facts: Addison formally introduces himself to Eve, escorts her away from Margo, and positions himself as her mentor or ally.
memories.memory_text: I saw Addison take Eve's arm and lead her away, and she gave me this uncertain smile as if she didn't know what was happening.

grounded_facts: Margo takes the coffee Birdie brings, transfers the olive from her martini into it, and waves her away without thanks.
memories.memory_text: I took the coffee Birdie brought me, dropped the olive from my martini into it, and waved her away without saying thanks.

grounded_facts: Margo insists the pianist replay 'Liebestraum' despite having played it four times, asserting control over the party's atmosphere.
memories.memory_text: I told the pianist to play 'Liebestraum' again, even though he had already played it several times, because I wanted to keep the feeling in the room exactly as it was.

grounded_facts: A post-gala gathering at Margo's home that has devolved into a quiet, melancholic state with only a few guests remaining.
memories.memory_text: I remember the quiet that settled in after the gala, with only a few guests left and the mood turning melancholy around me.

grounded_facts: Bill jokingly asks when guests can view the body, prompting Margo's serious response about her own emotional death.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill whispering to me about guests wanting to view the body, as if it were a joke, but it made me realize how I truly feel.

grounded_facts: Margo metaphorically identifies herself as a corpse undergoing embalming, expressing deep existential despair.
memories.memory_text: I told Bill I'm the remains of Margo Channing, still being embalmed, because that's how I feel—emotionally dead, sitting up for the last time.

grounded_facts: Margo explicitly tells Max she loves him, reinforcing their bond in a moment of emotional vulnerability.
memories.memory_text: I told Max I love him, and I really meant it, then I took his hand and led him to the pantry so we could be together away from the others.

grounded_facts: Margo offers Max bicarbonate for his heartburn, using the gesture to affirm their friendship and loyalty.
memories.memory_text: I offered Max bicarbonate for his heartburn and told him we'd put his name on the box in the pantry, just for him, to show how much I care about our friendship and loyalty.

grounded_facts: Margo locates the bicarbonate of soda in the cupboard and provides it to Max.
memories.memory_text: I found the bicarbonate of soda in the cupboard and gave it to Max, telling him it would help with his indigestion.

grounded_facts: Margo proposes to help Max by reading with Miss Caswell for her audition.
memories.memory_text: I proposed to Max that I read with Miss Caswell for her audition, telling him it was anything to help him out.

grounded_facts: Margo asks Max to give Eve a job in his office as a favor.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Margo asks Max to give Eve a job in his office as a favor.

grounded_facts: Under Margo's insistence, Max promises to give Eve Harrington a job in his office.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Under Margo's insistence, Max promises to give Eve Harrington a job in his office.

grounded_facts: Margo reveals she is forty years old, marking a moment of personal vulnerability and self-awareness.
memories.memory_text: I told Lloyd the truth about my age—I said, 'Three months ago, I was forty years old. Forty. Four oh,' and it felt like a weight lifting, even though it made me vulnerable.

grounded_facts: Lloyd suggests Margo's distress about age is actually about a fight with Bill.
memories.memory_text: Lloyd told me that my distress wasn't really about age, that it had everything to do with a fight I'd had with Bill, but I'm not sure he understood how much this role challenges who I am now.

grounded_facts: A private moment in the pantry after a party, where key personal and professional decisions are made.
memories.memory_text: After the party, I had a quiet moment in the pantry with Max where I offered to help him by reading with Miss Caswell for her audition, and we talked about important things, including my role in his life and my feelings about age and playing Cora.

grounded_facts: Despite her reservations about age, Margo decides to accept the role of Cora in Lloyd's play.
memories.memory_text: I decided to accept the role of Cora, so I told Lloyd, 'Don't worry, I'll play your play,' even if it means wearing rompers and rolling a hoop—I'm committing to this, despite my doubts.

grounded_facts: Eve speaks about the emotional reward of being loved by audiences nightly.
memories.memory_text: I heard Eve speak about how it feels to be loved by audiences every night, imagining the smiles and shining eyes as something worth any sacrifice.

grounded_facts: Margo exits a cab in front of the theater and enters the building on a Friday afternoon when there is no performance.
memories.memory_text: I got out of a cab in front of the theater and went inside on a Friday afternoon when there was no performance scheduled.

grounded_facts: The audition for Miss Caswell's role has already concluded by the time Margo arrives.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at the theater to support Miss Caswell, but Addison told me the audition was already over—it’s nearly four, and they had called it for 2:30.

grounded_facts: Addison informs Margo that Eve Harrington has been appointed as her understudy, replacing the pregnant previous candidate.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Addison that Eve Harrington had been named my understudy, replacing the previous one who was pregnant.

grounded_facts: Margo presses Addison to reveal who read with Miss Caswell, showing growing concern and suspicion.
memories.memory_text: I pressed Addison to tell me who read with Miss Caswell, feeling my concern grow as he spoke about Eve with such admiration.

grounded_facts: A scheduled theatrical audition originally set for 2:30 PM at the Curran Theater, where Eve Harrington delivered a standout performance.
memories.memory_text: I was told the audition had been scheduled for 2:30 at the Curran Theater, and that Eve Harrington gave a performance Addison compared to legendary actresses like Jeanne Eagels.

grounded_facts: Addison describes Eve's reading as a transcendent performance that deeply impressed him and Lloyd.
Addison passionately describes Eve's audition as a revelation, implicitly contrasting it with Margo's style.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Addison that Eve Harrington's reading wasn't just a reading but a performance—brilliant, vivid, something made of music and fire—and that she'd be among the rare ones who give a revelation like Jeanne Eagels or Helen Hayes, and I couldn't help but feel he was contrasting her with me, an old kazoo and some sparkles.

grounded_facts: Addison tells Miss Caswell to move to television, effectively ending her theater aspirations.
Addison suggests Miss Caswell pursue television instead of theater, implying her stage prospects are limited.
memories.memory_text: I heard Addison tell Miss Caswell she should move to television, implying her stage career wasn't going anywhere.

grounded_facts: Margo arrives late to the theater after the audition has concluded, unaware of Eve's new role.
memories.memory_text: I arrived late to the theater and didn't know the audition had already ended.

grounded_facts: Margo sarcastically references a promise Max made, implying he broke it by hiring Eve.
memories.memory_text: I sarcastically reminded Max about the promise he made, implying he broke it by hiring Eve, and said I kept my promise too.

grounded_facts: An audition was held for the role, featuring Eve and Miss Caswell, which concluded before Margo arrived.
memories.memory_text: I was told the audition was over, and that it had already concluded with Eve and Miss Caswell.

grounded_facts: Margo discovers that Eve has been appointed as her understudy without her knowledge.
memories.memory_text: I was told Eve had been made my understudy over a week ago, and I couldn't believe I hadn't known about it.

grounded_facts: Eve claims she could not have performed if Margo had been present, subtly undermining Margo's presence.
memories.memory_text: I heard Eve say she couldn't have performed if I'd been there, and that she would've stopped if I'd walked in.

grounded_facts: Lloyd blames Margo for turning a misunderstanding into a dramatic confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Lloyd blame me for turning a misunderstanding into a dramatic confrontation, saying I played a childish game.

grounded_facts: Margo threatens to leave the production, prompting Max to warn of legal consequences under her contract.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Mr. Fabian when he questioned whether I was breaking my contract, because I felt he was threatening me with legal action over my decision to leave the production.

grounded_facts: After the confrontation, both Lloyd and Max leave the theater, signaling a breakdown in professional relationships.
memories.memory_text: I saw both Lloyd and Max walk out of the theater after our argument, and I knew things had fallen apart between us.

grounded_facts: Margo accuses Lloyd of being overly impressed by Eve's performance, interpreting it as a personal attack.
memories.memory_text: I accused Lloyd of being too impressed by Eve's performance, which I saw as a personal attack on me and my work.

grounded_facts: Bill physically restrains Margo and declares his love, attempting to ground her emotionally.
Bill physically restrains Margo to stop her from continuing her outburst, asserting emotional control.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill grabbing me and pulling me down on the bed, holding me down to stop my outburst—he said I was hurting myself and him with my tantrums, and then he told me he loves me, called me a beautiful and intelligent woman and a great actress, said I have every reason to be happy.

grounded_facts: Bill asks Margo if marrying him would be enough to resolve her doubts, framing it as a final attempt to save the relationship.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill asking if marrying him would be enough to resolve my doubts, as if it were a final attempt to save us, and I told him I wouldn't want him to marry me just to prove something.

grounded_facts: Bill challenges Margo to reveal the real reason behind her behavior, accusing her of knowing but refusing to admit her true feelings.
memories.memory_text: I recall Bill pressing me, saying I must know the real reason behind my hesitation but won't admit it—accusing me of refusing to tell him the truth about how I feel.

grounded_facts: As Bill leaves, Margo calls out and asks if he is going to find Eve, reigniting the jealousy that fueled the conflict.
memories.memory_text: As he was leaving, I called out and asked if he was going to find Eve, and I saw the pain in his face when he said that made everything suddenly believable.

grounded_facts: Bill declares that his attempt to reconcile is his last, and he leaves Margo after she fails to respond to his plea for honesty and change.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill telling me this was his last try, that he had nothing else to offer, and then walking out when I couldn't answer—leaving me alone, and I began to cry.

grounded_facts: After Bill leaves, Margo, alone on stage, begins to cry, signaling emotional collapse.
memories.memory_text: After Bill left, I stayed on stage alone and began to cry.

grounded_facts: Lloyd praises Eve's talent and potential as an actress while speaking to Karen, implicitly criticizing Margo.
Lloyd shifts tone and speaks admiringly of Eve, contrasting her talent and potential with Margo's ego and resistance to change.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Lloyd praised Eve as a 'born actress' with sensitivity and vibrancy, saying she has everything, while also commenting that I'm great but that's the problem because I know it.

grounded_facts: Lloyd returns home angry after a confrontation with Margo, criticizing her unprofessionalism and emotional outbursts during the audition.
memories.memory_text: I saw Lloyd come home furious after his confrontation with me, slamming the door and ranting about my behavior during the audition, saying no one would give me the 'boot in the rear' I deserve.

grounded_facts: Karen informs Lloyd that they are planning a weekend trip to the country with Bill and Margo.
memories.memory_text: I heard Karen mention to Lloyd that we're planning a weekend trip to the country with Bill, him, and me, just the four of us.

grounded_facts: Karen places a phone call to Eve Harrington, marking the beginning of direct engagement.
memories.memory_text: I picked up the phone, looked in the book, dialed, and said, 'Hello... will you call Miss Eve Harrington to the phone, please?'

grounded_facts: After internal deliberation, Karen resolves that her idea is both harmless and beneficial, and initiates contact with Eve Harrington by phone.
memories.memory_text: I told myself it was just a harmless joke that would do more good than harm, and that Margo would even enjoy it eventually, so I decided to go through with it.

grounded_facts: The car stops functioning due to an empty fuel tank, stranding the group on a remote road.
memories.memory_text: The car suddenly slowed and came to a stop with that unmistakable hissing sound—no gas. I heard Karen protest that she’d filled the tank just yesterday, and Lloyd admit he hadn’t checked it this morning. It was clear: we were stranded on a remote road because the fuel tank was empty.

grounded_facts: A journey to deliver Margo to the train station in time for her theater performance.
memories.memory_text: I was anxious about making it to the train station in time for my theater performance, so when the others were discussing our progress, I asked how far we still had to go, knowing every minute counted.

grounded_facts: Lloyd chooses to leave the car and walk half a mile to seek assistance or find fuel.
memories.memory_text: Seeing no other option, Lloyd decided to walk about half a mile to find help. I watched him get out of the car, the cold rushing in, and then start down the icy road—he slipped once, caught himself, waved, and kept going.

grounded_facts: Margo acknowledges her unpleasant behavior and apologizes sincerely to Karen.
Margo admits she has been unpleasant recently and expresses genuine remorse, especially toward Karen and Lloyd.
memories.memory_text: I admitted to Karen that I haven't been pleasant lately and apologized sincerely, especially to her and Lloyd, because I truly regret how I've been behaving.

grounded_facts: Margo confesses her fear that Bill loves her persona, not her true self, and questions who she is beyond her fame.
Margo reveals her fear that Bill loves her public persona, not her authentic self.
memories.memory_text: I confessed to Karen that I'm afraid Bill loves Margo Channing, not the real me, and I don't even know who I am beneath the persona—I worry that when the fame fades, there might be nothing left.

grounded_facts: Karen expresses deep regret for not checking the gas level, which led to the breakdown.
Karen apologizes sincerely for her role in the car running out of gas, taking personal responsibility.
memories.memory_text: I remember Karen telling me how sorry she was about the car running out of gas, admitting she hadn't checked the fuel level and taking responsibility for it.

grounded_facts: The group is immobilized in a cold, isolated location after the car runs out of gas, leading to intimate conversation.
memories.memory_text: After the car stopped with a hiss, signaling we were out of gas, I stayed behind with Karen in the cold, isolated road. We wrapped the fur robe around us for warmth, I turned on the radio—first to 'Liebestraum,' then later to a piano nocturne—and eventually took out cigarettes, offering one to Karen. We lit up and settled in, snuggling into our furs as the silence between us softened into something more intimate.

grounded_facts: Addison overhears Bill complimenting Margo on her performance, calling her 'better than all right' and saying she 'rang a bell'.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bill say I was 'better than all right' and that I 'rang a bell' during my performance.

grounded_facts: Karen exits a taxi and enters the '21' Club in New York.
memories.memory_text: I saw Karen get out of a taxi and go into the '21' Club in New York.

grounded_facts: Karen expresses feelings of guilt and shame about Eve's performance being publicized.
memories.memory_text: I remember Karen telling me she felt terribly guilty and ashamed about Eve's performance being publicized.

grounded_facts: Margo reads Addison's column aloud in her living room, reacting with anger and distress as Karen and later Bill witness her response.
Margo expresses escalating anger while reading the column, directing her emotional reaction toward Karen as a witness.
memories.memory_text: I read Addison's column aloud in my living room, my hands shaking as I paced, and I could feel my anger building with every word—I saw Karen sitting there, watching me, but I couldn't stop myself from reacting.

grounded_facts: Margo declares her intent to take personal action against Eve and Addison deWitt in response to the column.
memories.memory_text: I declared that if Equity or my lawyer won't act, I'll personally make Eve and Addison pay for what they've done—I said I'd stuff that little lost lamb down deWitt's throat myself.

grounded_facts: Margo reads aloud from Addison's column that criticizes mature actresses and highlights Eve's accusations, leading to her outrage.
memories.memory_text: I read how Addison mocked mature actresses and praised Eve’s accusations, and I knew it was a direct attack on me—I felt it in my bones when I said those words out loud.

grounded_facts: Bill arrives at Margo's apartment after reading the column and physically comforts her as she breaks down.
Bill physically embraces Margo and verbally reassures her after her emotional breakdown.
memories.memory_text: I broke down when Bill arrived right after reading that awful column, and I remember him taking me in his arms and saying, 'Bill's here, baby. Everything's all right, now,' as he held me and comforted me.

grounded_facts: Karen acknowledges her presence is superfluous and exits the scene after Bill arrives and comforts Margo.
memories.memory_text: I was so overwhelmed that I barely noticed Karen, but I recall her saying something about being 'de trop' before she left, acknowledging she didn't belong in that moment between me and Bill.

grounded_facts: Lloyd informs Karen that Eve visited him and tried to explain her actions, but became emotional and couldn't finish.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Eve visited Lloyd and tried to explain her interview, but she became emotional and couldn't finish what she wanted to say.

grounded_facts: Eve visited Lloyd before Karen arrived, during which she attempted to explain her interview and apologized indirectly, mentioning the play 'Footsteps on the Ceiling'.
memories.memory_text: I think Eve came to see Lloyd before Karen arrived and tried to explain her interview, indirectly apologizing and mentioning 'Footsteps on the Ceiling,' but I wasn't there and only pieced this together afterward.

grounded_facts: Margo and Bill invite Lloyd and Karen to meet them at the Cub Room after the theater for wine, signaling a return to camaraderie.
memories.memory_text: I remember inviting Lloyd and Karen to meet us at the Cub Room after the theater for wine, which felt like a return to our usual camaraderie.

grounded_facts: After a phone call, Lloyd informs Karen that Margo and Bill want to meet them at the Cub Room after the theater.
memories.memory_text: I called Lloyd and invited him and Karen to meet Bill and me at the Cub Room after the theater for a bottle of wine, and I remember him saying they'd love to come.

grounded_facts: Lloyd reveals he has considered casting Eve Harrington in the lead role of 'Footsteps on the Ceiling', inspired during Eve's visit where she discussed the play.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Lloyd considered casting Eve in 'Footsteps on the Ceiling' after she mentioned the play during her visit, though he said he wouldn't make any change without Karen's approval.

grounded_facts: After the argument, Lloyd clarifies that he did not promise Eve the role and cited Karen's opposition as a key reason.
memories.memory_text: I heard from Lloyd that he didn't promise Eve the role and told her I was set on Margo playing it, and that he wouldn't make any casting change without my approval.

grounded_facts: A celebratory dinner at the Stork Club following Margo's acclaimed performance, attended by Margo, Bill, Lloyd, and Karen.
memories.memory_text: I was at a celebratory dinner at the Stork Club with Bill, Lloyd, and Karen after my performance, and we were all in high spirits.

grounded_facts: Bill praises Margo's performance in strong terms, calling it unique and unforgettable.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bill praise my performance in strong terms, saying he had never seen anything like it and that it was unforgettable.

grounded_facts: Bill interrupts Lloyd to sincerely propose a toast to Margo as his bride-to-be, marking a public declaration of their engagement.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill interrupting Lloyd to propose a sincere toast to me, declaring me his bride-to-be and announcing our plans to go to City Hall the next day.

grounded_facts: Margo and Bill reveal they will obtain a marriage license the next day at City Hall, initiating formal wedding proceedings.
memories.memory_text: I confirmed to Bill that I’ll meet him at City Hall tomorrow at ten to get our marriage license, just as he planned.

grounded_facts: Lloyd expresses disappointment at the City Hall plan and suggests a more elaborate wedding with cathedral and bishop.
memories.memory_text: I heard Lloyd say that City Hall was too plain for us and that he could picture me in a cathedral with a bishop and banks of flowers.

grounded_facts: Upon receiving Eve's note, Karen angrily dismisses any interest in what Eve might say.
memories.memory_text: I saw Karen react with anger when Eve's note came, dismissing whatever Eve had to say as nonsense, and I could tell she wanted nothing to do with it.

grounded_facts: Eve Harrington sends a discreet note to Karen Richards, requesting an urgent meeting in the Ladies' Room during the celebration.
memories.memory_text: I received a note from Eve Harrington asking me to meet her urgently in the Ladies' Room, and I remember how she underlined the word 'please' like it was some dramatic plea.

grounded_facts: Margo notices Addison DeWitt seated nearby with signs that Eve had been with him, revealing their connection.
memories.memory_text: I spotted Addison DeWitt sitting near the entrance at a table for two, and I could see clear signs that Eve had been there—her wine glass and a crumpled napkin—so I knew they'd been together.

grounded_facts: As Karen passes his table, Addison rises and greets her warmly, but she ignores him.
memories.memory_text: I saw Karen walk past Addison's table, and even though he stood up and greeted her warmly, saying 'Karen! How nice...', she completely ignored him and kept walking.

grounded_facts: Eve explicitly demands that Karen tell Lloyd she should play Cora, framing it as the most important thing Karen can do.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Eve explicitly demands that Karen tell Lloyd she should play Cora, framing it as the most important thing Karen can do.

grounded_facts: A private, emotionally charged conversation between Eve and Karen in the outer room of the Stork Club ladies' room.
memories.memory_text: I was present when Eve and Karen had a private, emotionally charged conversation in the outer room of the Stork Club ladies' room.

grounded_facts: Eve admits to Karen that her actions were influenced by Addison deWitt, acknowledging her own responsibility and disgrace.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Eve admitted to Karen that her actions were influenced by Addison deWitt, though I didn't hear the full extent of what she said.

grounded_facts: Eve reveals she knows Karen helped her cover Margo's absence and warns that Addison could expose the truth.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Eve reveals she knows Karen helped her cover Margo's absence and warns that Addison could expose the truth.

grounded_facts: Eve threatens to expose Karen's complicity in covering up Margo's missed performance, leveraging Addison's knowledge to force Karen into supporting her for the role of Cora.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Eve threatens to expose Karen's complicity in covering up Margo's missed performance, leveraging Addison's knowledge to force Karen into supporting her for the role of Cora.

grounded_facts: As Eve and Addison leave, Margo derides Eve as 'Eve evil, Little Miss Evil', reasserting dominance through theatrical scorn.
memories.memory_text: As Eve and Addison left, I called her 'Eve evil, Little Miss Evil' to reassert my dominance through mockery.

grounded_facts: Margo publicly declares she forgives Eve, linking her happiness to the group's unity, which she attributes to Eve's actions.
memories.memory_text: I forgave Eve publicly because I realized her actions led to the four of us being together like this, and I linked my happiness to our unity, which I said was her doing.

grounded_facts: Margo shares her vision of domestic life and marriage with Karen, referencing shared memories.
memories.memory_text: I told Karen about my dream of having a real home and a man to come home to, and I asked her if she remembered, because we'd talked about such things before.

grounded_facts: Margo declares she no longer wants to play 'Cora', citing her new married life and personal fulfillment as reasons.
memories.memory_text: I told Lloyd I don't want to play 'Cora' anymore because I finally have a life to live, and I don't need to act in roles I'm too old for just to fill my nights.

grounded_facts: After Margo rejects the role of Cora, Karen bursts into uncontrollable laughter, masking complex emotions.
memories.memory_text: After I said I wouldn't play Cora, I saw Karen burst into hysterical laughter, and it felt like she was hiding something behind it.

grounded_facts: A celebratory late-night gathering at the Cub Room where the group, including Margo and Bill on their wedding night, celebrates with champagne and conversation.
memories.memory_text: I remember that joyful night at the Cub Room, celebrating with Bill on our wedding night, feeling the warmth of champagne and the company of friends around me. I looked around and thought how lovely it was, how all those elite eyes were on me, and I even forgave Eve for what she’d done—because in that moment, I had everything: a home, a man to come home to, and a life that no longer needed the stage. I made sure Karen saw it too, when I took her glass away.

grounded_facts: Eve retrieves Bill and persuades him to continue the rehearsal despite the conflict.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Eve went after Bill and brought him back, convincing him to continue with the rehearsal despite the conflict.

grounded_facts: A rehearsal of the play where Eve performs a scene and conflicts arise between Bill and Lloyd over staging decisions.
memories.memory_text: I was told that during the rehearsal, Eve performed her scene and there was a conflict between Bill and Lloyd over how things should be staged.

grounded_facts: From the stage, Eve whispers to Lloyd, calming him after the conflict with Bill.
memories.memory_text: I learned that after the argument, Eve whispered to Lloyd from the stage and calmed him down, getting him to sit back down and carry on.

grounded_facts: After a confrontation with Lloyd, Bill storms offstage, abandoning the rehearsal momentarily.
memories.memory_text: I heard that Bill stormed offstage after his fight with Lloyd, throwing his script and leaving the rehearsal for a while.

grounded_facts: A formal event honoring Eve with the Sarah Siddons Award, attended by theater figures and hosted by Max Fabian.
Eve is formally presented with the Sarah Siddons Award by the Aged Actor and delivers a public acceptance speech.
memories.memory_text: I attended the formal event where Eve was presented with the Sarah Siddons Award by the Aged Actor and delivered her acceptance speech, which began with humble words about being an apprentice in the theater.

grounded_facts: Eve publicly thanks Max Fabian for giving her a chance as an unknown actress.
memories.memory_text: I heard Eve thank Max Fabian during her speech, calling him 'dear, sentimental, generous, courageous Max' for giving her a chance when she was an unknown actress.

grounded_facts: Eve thanks Karen as her first friend in the theater.
memories.memory_text: I remember Eve thanking Karen as her first friend in the theater, and I saw Karen react with a quiet smile while doodling as the applause came.

grounded_facts: Eve names Margo Channing as her idol and benefactor.
memories.memory_text: I was named by Eve as my idol and benefactor during her speech, and though the audience applauded, I could only manage a grim smile in response.

grounded_facts: Eve thanks Bill Sampson for his direction and patience.
memories.memory_text: I heard Eve thank Bill Sampson for his direction and patience, acknowledging he demanded more than she could give but taught her well.

grounded_facts: Eve acknowledges Lloyd Richards for writing the play and believing in her.
memories.memory_text: I listened as Eve expressed deep gratitude to Lloyd Richards for writing the play and believing in her, asking how she could ever repay him.

grounded_facts: Eve reveals her upcoming move to Hollywood to make a film, while affirming her emotional commitment to theater.
memories.memory_text: I heard Eve announce she would be moving to Hollywood to make a film, though she claimed her heart would always remain in the theater.

grounded_facts: Karen offers a brief, formal congratulation to Eve after the speech.
memories.memory_text: I saw Karen offer a brief, formal congratulations to Eve right after the speech.

grounded_facts: A high-class party hosted by Max Fabian in honor of Eve's award, planned to follow the ceremony.
memories.memory_text: I learned from Max Fabian that he was hosting a high-class party for Eve after the ceremony, and he made a comment about her not needing to be late like at a rehearsal.

grounded_facts: Margo delivers a sarcastic comment questioning Eve's emotional authenticity.
Margo responds to Eve's speech with a biting comment implying Eve lacks genuine emotion.
memories.memory_text: I delivered a sarcastic remark to Eve after her speech, implying she lacks genuine emotion—her heart won't be missed since she can put the award where it should be.

grounded_facts: Eve hands her Sarah Siddons Award to Addison, symbolically rejecting its value or her connection to the celebration.
memories.memory_text: I handed my Sarah Siddons Award to Addison and told him to take it to the party instead of me, symbolizing that I didn't care about the celebration or what the award represented anymore.

grounded_facts: After the ceremony, Eve decides not to attend the celebratory party hosted by Max Fabian.
memories.memory_text: I remember deciding not to go to Max's party after the ceremony because I just wanted to go home, and when Addison reminded me how much trouble Max had gone to, I told him it wasn't really for me—it was for the award, and I was tired and wanted to leave.

grounded_facts: A formal annual gathering of the Sarah Siddons Society to celebrate distinguished achievement in theater, culminating in the presentation of the Sarah Siddons Award.
memories.memory_text: I was at the annual banquet of the Sarah Siddons Society, where they gather to honor distinguished achievement in theater.

grounded_facts: Addison narrates an introduction of Karen Richards, framing her as connected to the theater only through marriage, subtly undermining her legitimacy.
memories.memory_text: I heard Addison introduce Karen Richards as connected to the theater only by marriage, as if that made her involvement less legitimate.

grounded_facts: Addison asserts Margo Channing's enduring stardom and centrality to the theater, while simultaneously noting she was passed over for the award-winning role.
memories.memory_text: I was told I'm still considered a true Star of the theater, but also that the role Eve got the award for was originally meant for me.

grounded_facts: Addison deWitt reveals that the role for which Eve Harrington won the award was originally intended for Margo Channing, establishing a narrative contrast between the two figures.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Addison deWitt said the part Eve won the award for was originally meant for me, and I knew then how the story was being framed — not just about her rise, but about my being set aside.

grounded_facts: The aged actor delivers a ceremonial speech extolling Eve Harrington's youth, humility, devotion, and love for theater, justifying her receipt of the award.
memories.memory_text: I heard the aged actor give a speech praising Eve Harrington's youth, humility, and devotion to theater, saying her dream of belonging to us had come true.

grounded_facts: Eve Harrington is formally awarded the Sarah Siddons Award for Distinguished Achievement by the aged actor, marking her official recognition as a leading figure in the theater.
memories.memory_text: I saw the aged actor present the Sarah Siddons Award to Eve Harrington, and I watched her rise gracefully to accept it amid applause.

grounded_facts: Margo does not applaud Eve's award moment, not as a deliberate snub but indicating her mind is elsewhere, signaling emotional distance or preoccupation.
memories.memory_text: I didn't applaud when Eve got her award—not because I meant to snub her, but because my mind was somewhere else, caught up in my own thoughts.

grounded_facts: Addison stops applauding and shifts his gaze from Margo to Karen, then back to Eve, signaling his awareness of their emotional states and positioning himself as a narrative controller.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Addison stop applauding and shift his gaze between Karen and me before fixing it back on Eve, as if he were measuring our reactions and reminding us he's the one telling this story.

memories.memory_text: I starred in 'Aged in Wood,' a play presented by Max Fabian and written by Lloyd Richards, and the performance has just ended.
