memories.memory_text: I exited my taxi and entered the alley behind the theater where my show was playing, looking around curiously before making my way in.

grounded_facts: Karen decides to bring Eve to meet Margo Channing after learning about her devotion as a fan.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Karen decided to bring Eve to meet me after hearing how devoted she was as a fan.

grounded_facts: Karen and Eve arrive at the backstage of the Curran Theater at night, with Karen leading the way to Margo's dressing room.
memories.memory_text: I saw Karen and Eve arrive backstage at the Curran Theater at night, with Karen leading the way to my dressing room.

grounded_facts: Eve and Karen arrive outside Margo's dressing room at the Curran Theater, where they hear Margo's voice from inside.
Karen and Eve arrive at Margo's dressing room backstage at the Curran Theater during the night.
memories.memory_text: I arrived with Karen at my dressing room backstage at the Curran Theater at night, and I remember my loud guffaw making us pause as Eve and Karen approached.

grounded_facts: Margo contemptuously rejects the idea that autograph seekers are her real audience, calling them delinquents and 'nobody's fans'.
memories.memory_text: I told Karen that autograph seekers aren't real people—they're nobody's fans, just juvenile delinquents and mental detectives who never even see the plays.

grounded_facts: Karen reveals that Eve has been waiting outside Margo's dressing room and insists that Margo meet her.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Karen that Eve had been waiting just outside my dressing room, and she insisted I meet her.

grounded_facts: Eve enters the dressing room and is formally introduced to Margo, Lloyd, and Birdie.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve come into my dressing room, and Karen introduced her to me, Lloyd, and Birdie.

grounded_facts: Margo instantly adopts a gracious, theatrical persona upon Eve's entrance, welcoming her with exaggerated warmth.
memories.memory_text: I adopted a gracious, theatrical manner when Eve entered and welcomed her with warm, musical words, saying, 'How do you do, my dear.'

grounded_facts: A private gathering in Margo's dressing room after a theater performance, involving conversation, drinks, and social dynamics among Margo, her inner circle, and a visiting fan.
memories.memory_text: I was in my dressing room after the performance, still in my wrapper with my wig off, having a drink and talking with my inner circle when a visiting fan came by—Birdie was there, loyal as ever, and I remember shifting into my first-lady-of-the-theater manner when the moment called for it.

grounded_facts: Eve tells Lloyd and Margo that she has attended every performance and lives for theater because of Margo.
memories.memory_text: I remember Eve telling me and Lloyd that she had seen every single performance of mine, and how her life revolved around the theater because of me—she even followed me from San Francisco to the East Coast just to keep watching my work.

grounded_facts: Eve begins to share her background, explaining her deep emotional connection to Margo's performances and her isolated life centered around theater, including her impoverished upbringing, work as a secretary, marriage to Eddie, his death in the war, and her emotional connection to Margo's performance in 'Remembrance' that led her to stay in San Francisco.
memories.memory_text: I recall Eve sharing her past with us—how she grew up alone in Wisconsin, found escape in acting and make-believe, worked as a secretary in a brewery, lost her husband Eddie in the war, and stayed in San Francisco after seeing me perform in 'Remembrance,' which changed her life.

grounded_facts: Margo sharply rebukes Birdie for mocking Eve's emotional story, asserting the dignity of personal grief.
memories.memory_text: I told Birdie that some human experiences aren't for mocking in a vaudeville house, and that even she should respect genuine grief.

grounded_facts: Birdie directly apologizes to Eve for her sarcastic remark, acknowledging her feelings.
memories.memory_text: I saw Birdie apologize to Eve, saying she was sorry for hurting her feelings and that it was just her way of talking.

grounded_facts: After mocking Eve's story, Birdie acknowledges her insensitivity and offers a direct apology, marking a shift in her attitude.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Birdie apologize to Eve after mocking her story, acknowledging her insensitivity and marking a shift in her attitude.

grounded_facts: Bill enters abruptly and disrupts the intimate atmosphere with his urgent, theatrical complaints about being late.
Bill enters the dressing room abruptly, announcing his imminent departure and creating a shift in the gathering's dynamics.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill bursting into my dressing room, suitcase in hand, complaining about being late and my lack of readiness—he said his plane was leaving soon and called me a junk yard, which stung, though he tried to soften it by calling me his 'wonderful junk yard.'

grounded_facts: Margo personally asks Eve to remain after others leave, signaling special interest and emotional connection.
memories.memory_text: I asked Eve to stay after the others left, telling her we could put Stanislavsky on his plane and then go somewhere to talk, because I wanted a real conversation with her.

grounded_facts: After initially preparing to leave, Eve agrees to remain with Margo after being personally invited to continue their conversation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve hesitate at first, but then she agreed to stay when I invited her, saying she didn’t want to be in the way.

grounded_facts: Karen tells Eve she hopes to see her not just as a fan, but as a friend, extending social inclusion.
memories.memory_text: I saw Karen say to Eve, 'I hope I see you again soon—not just that way. As a friend,' which felt like a genuine moment of connection beyond fandom.

grounded_facts: Eve tells Karen she will never forget the night or her role in making it possible, emphasizing emotional impact.
memories.memory_text: I heard Eve tell Karen, 'I'll never forget this night as long as I live. And I'll never forget you for making it possible,' which struck me as deeply sincere.

grounded_facts: Karen and Lloyd say goodbye to Eve and leave the gathering, marking the end of their participation in the occasion.
memories.memory_text: I watched Karen and Lloyd say their goodbyes—Karen told me good night and that she’d call tomorrow, then she and Lloyd left with Eve, marking the end of the gathering.

grounded_facts: Bill admits he lied about the time, indicating they will make it easily despite Eve's concern.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bill admit he lied about the time, saying we'd make it easily, and I couldn't help but think he was right—I really don't have any sense of time.

grounded_facts: Bill takes Margo's pocketbook, finds a letter she has carried for weeks, and admits to reading it three times.
memories.memory_text: I didn't realize Bill had taken my pocketbook and read the letter I've been carrying around for weeks—he admitted he'd read it three times, which shocked me.

grounded_facts: Bill passionately explains that theater exists beyond Broadway and includes film, justifying his decision to go to Hollywood.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bill passionately explain that theater isn't just Broadway—it includes film, rodeos, ballets, and even Donald Duck, saying magic and make-believe anywhere with an audience counts as Theater.

grounded_facts: Bill confirms his intention to accept a film deal in Hollywood, despite Eve's concern about few returning.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill confirm he wants to go to Hollywood, not because he has to, and even when Eve warned him few come back, he stood by his decision without needing her approval.

grounded_facts: Bill tells Margo to throw away her letter, calling it dreary and boring, undermining its emotional significance.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill telling me to throw that dreary thing away because it bored him.

grounded_facts: Margo cannot find her second earring and begins searching, initiating a minor disruption in departure plans.
memories.memory_text: I couldn't find my other earring, so I started searching and asked Birdie to look through the wigs in case it got caught.

grounded_facts: Margo tells Eve that Bill can't keep his eyes off her legs, creating a moment of shared amusement.
memories.memory_text: I told Eve that Bill couldn't keep his eyes off her legs, and we both laughed about it.

grounded_facts: Bill embraces Birdie and jokes about delivering messages to Tyrone Power, ending with mutual cheek kisses.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill embrace Birdie and joke about delivering a message to Tyrone Power, and then they exchanged cheek kisses.

grounded_facts: Margo retrieves the letter while searching for her earring and throws it away after Bill calls it dreary.
memories.memory_text: I found my letter while searching for my earring and ended up throwing it away after Bill called it dreary.

grounded_facts: A brief assembly in Margo's dressing room before leaving for another destination, involving conversation and last-minute preparations.
memories.memory_text: I remember putting on my earring and buzzing out of the bathroom with Birdie behind me, then sharing a moment with Bill before I took Eve's arm and we headed out the door together.

grounded_facts: Margo and Eve exit ahead of Bill, who shares a kiss with Birdie, marking the end of the gathering.
memories.memory_text: I walked out with Eve ahead of Bill, knowing he was sharing a kiss with Birdie before leaving.

grounded_facts: A structured travel event at LaGuardia Field where passengers check in for a flight; involves procedural logistics and emotional farewells.
memories.memory_text: I remember standing at LaGuardia Field with Bill and Eve, feeling the tension of the check-in process and knowing our time together was running short before the flight.

grounded_facts: Eve proactively offers to manage the check-in so Bill and Margo can have private time before departure.
Eve proposes to take care of the check-in procedures so Margo and Bill can spend their last moments together before departure.
memories.memory_text: I was told Eve offered to handle the check-in so Bill and I could have a few private moments before departure, which I appreciated.

grounded_facts: With Eve taking over the check-in task, Bill and Margo are freed to spend their final moments together before boarding.
memories.memory_text: Because Eve took over the check-in, I was able to spend our final moments with Bill without worrying about the logistics.

grounded_facts: Margo smiles gratefully at Eve after she takes on the check-in task.
memories.memory_text: I smiled gratefully at Eve after she took on the check-in task, glad for her help in that moment.

grounded_facts: Bill accepts Eve's offer by handing her the ticket, transferring responsibility for check-in.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill hand the ticket to Eve, accepting her offer and passing the responsibility to her.

grounded_facts: Margo tells Bill not to get stuck on some 'glamour puss,' expressing concern over his vulnerability to superficial attractions.
memories.memory_text: I told Bill not to get stuck on some 'glamour puss,' because I worry he might be drawn to someone flashy and shallow.

grounded_facts: Margo directly asks Bill if she is going to lose him, revealing her emotional dependence and anxiety.
memories.memory_text: I asked Bill, 'Am I going to lose you, Bill? Am I?'—I couldn't hold back how scared I am of losing him.

grounded_facts: Bill begins to kiss Margo but stops immediately when he notices Eve nearby, indicating a shift in attention and emotional tension.
memories.memory_text: I felt Bill start to kiss me, but he stopped suddenly when he noticed Eve standing nearby, and it left me feeling exposed and interrupted in that moment.

grounded_facts: A moment at LaGuardia airport where Bill, Margo, and Eve prepare for Bill's departure, marked by emotional exchanges and logistical actions.
memories.memory_text: I remember handing Bill his ticket at LaGuardia and walking with him toward the gate, knowing our moment was ending.

grounded_facts: Eve hands Bill his ticket and announces they are ready, asserting her role in the travel group and her proximity to Bill.
Eve hands Bill his ticket, signaling her involvement in the travel logistics and her presence as an active participant in the scene.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve hand Bill his ticket and announce they were ready, and I realized she was positioning herself right at the center of things, close to him and in control of the departure.

grounded_facts: Bill asks Eve to look after Margo, calling her a 'loose lamb in a jungle', implying emotional vulnerability.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Bill to have Eve keep an eye on me, like I'm a loose lamb in a jungle—he must think I can't handle things on my own.

grounded_facts: Bill boards the plane after saying goodbye to Margo and Eve, marking his physical departure from the scene.
A farewell gathering at the boarding gate as Bill departs on a flight.
memories.memory_text: I watched Bill pause and then wave before he climbed aboard the plane, closing the door behind him, as Eve stood with me at the gate for his farewell.

grounded_facts: After Bill leaves, Eve shifts from linking arms to placing her arm comfortingly around Margo, showing emotional support.
memories.memory_text: After Bill left, I felt lost, and Eve shifted from linking arms with me to putting her arm around me comfortingly as we walked away together.

grounded_facts: Addison offers Margo a drink; she declines absently, indicating preoccupation with her thoughts about Eve.
memories.memory_text: I was lost in thought about Eve, so when Addison offered me a drink, I barely noticed and just shook my head without really seeing him.

grounded_facts: Eve hands Margo a pen and stack of letters, takes the script from her, and facilitates her workflow without verbal exchange.
memories.memory_text: I handed my script to Eve, and without a word, she gave me a pen and a stack of letters to sign, taking the script from me so I could focus on the correspondence.

grounded_facts: Eve intercepts the phone call and skillfully rejects the caller, demonstrating control over access to Margo.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve get to the phone before Birdie and politely turn the caller away, handling things as if she were in charge.

grounded_facts: After Eve takes the phone call, Birdie glares at her, showing resentment toward Eve's growing influence.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Birdie glaring at Eve after the call, and then she looked at me, clearly upset about Eve stepping in.

grounded_facts: A quiet moment in Margo's living room where Eve assists with correspondence, Birdie serves tea, and Margo reads a script, forming a domestic but charged setting.
memories.memory_text: I was in my living room, relaxing by the fire with a script, when Eve brought me letters to sign, took the script from me, and Birdie served tea before giving us both a sharp look, making me lean back and close my eyes, savoring a quiet yet charged moment.

grounded_facts: After failing to answer the phone and witnessing Eve's behavior, Birdie slams the door as she leaves, expressing clear resentment.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting by the fire with my script when Birdie brought in tea, and after Eve took the call and I dismissed the caller, I saw Birdie slam the door on her way out, clearly upset.

memories.memory_text: I decided not to take another curtain call, feeling that applause had become just a habit rather than something meaningful.

grounded_facts: Eve emotionally declares she could watch Margo's performance repeatedly and cry each time, indicating intense personal investment.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Eve that she could watch my final scene a thousand times and still cry each time, which I took as a deep compliment.

grounded_facts: Eve points out deviations in staging since the director's absence, showing attention to detail and alignment with Margo's standards.
Eve criticizes the cast's deviation from original direction, implicitly supporting Margo's artistic integrity.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Eve that the cast has been changing things since the director left, and she pointed out how even Roger Ferraday has been moving closer during my scene, which shows she really notices what's right in a performance.

grounded_facts: Margo responds to Eve's observation about Roger Ferraday with a hyperbolic threat, maintaining rapport.
memories.memory_text: When Eve mentioned Roger Ferraday creeping closer each night, I joked that I'd spit in his eye if he got too close, just to keep things light and friendly between us.

grounded_facts: A post-performance curtain call at the Curran Theater where Margo receives sustained applause, followed by a private exchange with Eve.
memories.memory_text: I felt the warmth of the audience's sustained applause at the Curran Theater, and later shared a private moment with Eve as we went to my dressing room.

grounded_facts: Margo responds to Eve's emotional state with a grin and physical contact, guiding her toward the dressing room.
memories.memory_text: I grinned at Eve's emotional reaction and took her arm, guiding her with me toward my dressing room.

grounded_facts: Margo takes Eve's arm and they stroll to Margo's dressing room, marking a shift from public to private space.
memories.memory_text: I took Eve's arm and we walked to my dressing room together, where I started unhooking my gown with her help, moving from the stage into a more private moment.

grounded_facts: A private moment in Margo's dressing room after her stage performance, involving Eve and Birdie.
memories.memory_text: After my performance, I was in my dressing room with Birdie and Eve, and I could feel the new girdle was tighter—I told Birdie so, and Eve tried to help by offering to take my costume to the wardrobe mistress, though I appreciated the thought.

grounded_facts: Birdie indirectly alerts Margo that Eve’s action risks offending unionized wardrobe staff.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Birdie that wardrobe women are extremely touchy, next to tenors, and that they have strict duties—like carrying clothes and pressing them right—so letting someone else muscle in could cause trouble.

grounded_facts: Margo understands from Birdie's comment that Eve is encroaching on the wardrobe mistress's duties, which could cause conflict.
memories.memory_text: I realized Birdie’s comment meant Eve was stepping into the wardrobe mistress’s role, and I wasn’t sure how far that might go, but I thought it could spark conflict, so I hurried out after her.

grounded_facts: Eve picks up Margo's discarded costume and leaves the dressing room to deliver it, bypassing protocol.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve pick up my discarded costume and leave the room to deliver it herself, bypassing the usual protocol, so I hurried out after her to stop her before she caused any offense.

grounded_facts: Eve offers to take Margo's costume to the wardrobe mistress despite Margo telling her not to bother, subtly overstepping boundaries.
memories.memory_text: I told Eve not to bother taking my costume because Mrs. Brown would be along for it, but she ignored me and went anyway, overstepping after I’d already dismissed the idea.

grounded_facts: Eve holds Margo's dress against her body in front of mirrors, mimicking Margo's performance gestures, indicating identification with or aspiration to Margo's role.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve holding my dress against her body in front of the mirrors, turning and bowing just like me, as if she were performing for an audience.

grounded_facts: Margo uses indirect but clear language to reprimand Eve for overstepping by trying on her dress, asserting professional and symbolic boundaries.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve standing in front of the mirrors with my dress against her body, mimicking me, and I called out to stop her—I made it clear that such things aren't done.

grounded_facts: Margo quietly tells Eve that Mrs. Brown should handle the wardrobe, halting Eve's intimate engagement with her costume.
memories.memory_text: I quietly told Eve that I think we'd better let Mrs. Brown pick up the wardrobe, because it's not right for her to be handling my costume like that.

grounded_facts: Margo is awakened by a phone call from Bill, who reveals it is his birthday and that he expected her to remember the call they had planned for midnight.
memories.memory_text: I was asleep when the phone rang, and I fumbled to answer it, only to hear Bill's voice booming through the line, thrilled and insistent that I had called him at midnight for his birthday—though I hadn't, and I realized I'd forgotten it completely.

grounded_facts: Margo comes to the painful realization that she failed to remember or act on Bill's birthday, despite the planned midnight call.
memories.memory_text: I suddenly realized I hadn't remembered Bill's birthday or made the call—I just sat there, stunned, knowing it was too late and that I'd let him down.

grounded_facts: Bill insists that Margo say or sing 'Happy Birthday,' expressing disappointment when she resists.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill calling me at midnight, insisting I say or sing 'Happy Birthday'—he sounded disappointed when I hesitated, and I could tell he really wanted me to make it special, like those old Western Union singers.

grounded_facts: The occasion of Bill's birthday, marked by a scheduled midnight phone call and expectations of recognition from Margo.
memories.memory_text: I remember now—Bill expected me to remember his birthday and call at midnight, and when I finally said 'birthday and welcome home,' it felt like I was scrambling to catch up to something I should have already been part of.

grounded_facts: Bill informs Margo that Eve has been in regular contact since his departure, implying a closer connection between Eve and Bill than Margo anticipated.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Bill that Eve has been writing to him every week since he left and that she knew all about the party plans, even though I didn't know she was involved.

grounded_facts: Bill says 'I love you,' but Margo initially responds by muttering about checking with Eve, only repeating the phrase after being prompted.
memories.memory_text: When Bill said 'I love you,' I found myself muttering that I'd check with Eve, and only after he questioned me did I repeat 'I love you too' before ending the call.

grounded_facts: Margo directly questions Birdie about her feelings toward Eve, seeking honest feedback.
memories.memory_text: I looked at Birdie and asked directly—"You don't like Eve, do you?"—and though she tried to deflect, I pushed for the truth, and she finally admitted she didn't, confirming that I wasn't imagining the tension.

grounded_facts: Margo confronts Birdie about her dislike of Eve, seeking insight into Eve's true intentions and behavior.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Birdie about her dislike of Eve, pressing her for an honest answer, and when she finally spoke, she revealed that Eve watches me like I'm a play or a blueprint—studying every move, every habit, with cold precision, which only deepened my suspicions.

grounded_facts: Birdie suggests that Eve observes Margo with detached, analytical intensity, like studying a text or blueprint.
memories.memory_text: Birdie told me plainly: Eve studies me like I'm a set of blueprints—how I walk, talk, think, eat, sleep—like I'm an object to be decoded, not a person to be admired, and that moment crystallized all my unease into certainty.

grounded_facts: Eve informs Margo that she has handled several responsibilities, including returning a script and preparing tax documents.
memories.memory_text: I remember Eve telling me she had taken care of several things, like returning the script and preparing the tax documents, and I remarked that it seemed I couldn't think of anything she hadn't already handled.

grounded_facts: Eve admits she sent a telegram to Bill for his birthday without consulting Margo.
Eve discloses she sent a telegram to Bill for his birthday on Margo's behalf, without prior approval.
memories.memory_text: I recall Eve admitting she had sent a birthday telegram to Bill on my behalf without asking me first, and though I told her it was thoughtful, I felt uneasy about her overstepping.

grounded_facts: A domestic morning scene where Margo receives breakfast, discusses Eve with Birdie, and meets with Eve about daily tasks.
memories.memory_text: It was morning, I was in bed with breakfast, Birdie brought my tray and we began talking about Eve—then Eve arrived in a sharp new suit, full of updates and reminders, acting as if she’d already taken over my life, and afterward, I just sat there, staring at the door, wondering when I stopped being in control.

grounded_facts: Margo silently toasts Karen, creating a moment of mutual awareness between the two characters.
memories.memory_text: I raised my glass in a silent toast to Karen, and I felt a moment of quiet understanding between us.

grounded_facts: Karen reports that she saw Eve often but did not talk meaningfully until the party for Bill.
memories.memory_text: I heard Karen say that she saw Eve often but didn't have any real conversation with her until the party I gave for Bill after he came back from Hollywood.

grounded_facts: Eve effusively praises Margo Channing, emphasizing her gratitude and emotional connection to her mentor.
memories.memory_text: I remember Eve telling me how happy she was to be with me, saying there should be a new word for happiness and that I'd been so wonderful to her.

grounded_facts: Eve expresses her desire to become Margo's new understudy, citing her deep knowledge of the role and staging, and asks Karen to advocate for her with Mr. Fabian.
memories.memory_text: I heard Eve express to Karen that she wanted to become my understudy, saying she knows the part and staging so well that there'd be no need to bring in someone new, though she also said she wasn't sure she could go on in front of my audience, and then asked Karen to talk to Mr. Fabian about it.

grounded_facts: Karen affirms that Eve should be Margo's understudy and promises to speak to Mr. Fabian on her behalf, reinforcing Eve's aspirations.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Karen sees no reason why I shouldn't be Margo's understudy, and when I asked her to talk to Mr. Fabian about it, she promised she would and said she wouldn't forget.

grounded_facts: Addison corrects Miss Caswell's mistaken attempt to summon a butler as a waiter, then dismisses her defense as idiotic.
memories.memory_text: I heard Addison correct Miss Caswell when she called the butler a waiter, and then mock her for trying to defend it by saying you can't yell 'Oh, butler'—I remember thinking how harsh he was, though he seemed amused by his own remark.

grounded_facts: Eve interrupts the conversation to passionately affirm that being an actor is worth it for the applause and audience adoration, revealing her deep emotional investment in performance.
memories.memory_text: I heard Eve passionately declare that the applause alone—those waves of love from the audience—makes being an actor worth it, and I could feel how deeply she meant it.

grounded_facts: Karen challenges Margo's star behavior, telling her to treat guests as supporting cast rather than subjects of her drama.
memories.memory_text: I remember Karen telling me to stop being a star and to treat my guests as my supporting cast instead of subjects of my drama.

grounded_facts: Margo mocks Eve's deference by sarcastically suggesting she would undress and tuck her into bed, rejecting Eve's offer with contempt.
memories.memory_text: I mocked Eve when she offered to help me, sarcastically asking if she'd take my clothes off and tuck me in—then made it clear I wouldn't like that at all.

grounded_facts: After Margo's exit, Karen approaches Eve, puts an arm around her, and reassures her that Margo's behavior isn't her fault.
memories.memory_text: After I left, I recall Karen going to Eve, putting an arm around her, and saying she was fond of me but sometimes wanted to kick me right square in the pants, telling Eve not to take my behavior personally.

grounded_facts: A late-night informal gathering on the stairs after a party, where theater professionals discuss the nature of their community while tensions simmer beneath the surface.
memories.memory_text: I remember us all sitting on the stairs after the party, that late-night gathering where we talked and tensions simmered beneath the surface, and I told Addison to host his own party while Eve watched me closely before crossing over to him.

grounded_facts: Margo finishes dressing and puts on jewelry before the party, expressing premonition about the evening.
memories.memory_text: I finished dressing and was putting on my jewelry, sipping a martini, when I realized I had a bad feeling about the party.

grounded_facts: Birdie assists Margo by zipping the back of her dress, completing her outfit.
memories.memory_text: I asked Birdie to zip the back of my dress, and she did, saying 'Voila' as she finished.

grounded_facts: The period before Margo's party during which she finishes getting ready and receives updates about preparations.
Margo makes a sarcastic remark implying the guests are unpleasant and were a mistake to invite.
memories.memory_text: While I was getting ready and Birdie updated me on the party details, I remarked that the only thing I ordered by mistake was the guests.

grounded_facts: Margo expresses concern about Bill being late, only to learn from Birdie that he has already arrived twenty minutes ago.
memories.memory_text: I heard from Birdie that Bill had already been there for twenty minutes, which surprised me since he hadn't come to find me.

grounded_facts: Margo asks Birdie about Bill's whereabouts, concerned he is late for the party.
memories.memory_text: I asked Birdie where Bill was because I noticed he was late, and I remarked that it was odd he hadn't even come up to see me yet.

grounded_facts: Margo increases her pace while descending the stairs, indicating urgency or anxiety.
memories.memory_text: I increased my pace going down the stairs, feeling the urgency in my steps.

grounded_facts: Margo deliberately arrives at the second floor landing and begins moving toward the living room where Bill and Eve are conversing.
memories.memory_text: I deliberately arrived at the landing and started moving toward the living room where Bill and Eve were talking.

grounded_facts: Bill shares an anecdote with Eve, who chuckles in response, creating a moment of shared amusement.
memories.memory_text: I could hear Bill telling a story and making Eve laugh before I walked in, and I could tell they were enjoying themselves.

grounded_facts: Eve sees Margo approaching and stands up, interrupting her conversation with Bill.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Eve saw me coming and got to her feet right away, cutting off her conversation with Bill.

grounded_facts: Margo's deliberate arrival and approach disrupt the intimate moment between Bill and Eve.
memories.memory_text: I approached the living room and saw that my arrival disrupted the moment between Bill and Eve—Eve stood up and Bill turned toward me.

grounded_facts: Bill directly criticizes Margo for unfairly judging Eve and accuses her of paranoia.
Bill angrily dismisses Margo's suspicions about Eve, defending Eve's innocence and condemning Margo's paranoia.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill yelling at me, defending Eve and saying her adoration for me was genuine — he accused me of being paranoid and said I should be ashamed of suspecting her.

grounded_facts: Margo confronts Bill about his interaction with Eve, revealing her growing jealousy and insecurity about Eve's presence and admiration.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Bill about how he's been acting around Eve, because I could feel him pulling away and I wasn't going to sit quietly while he dismissed my concerns as jealousy.

grounded_facts: Eve enters the room and silently witnesses the end of Margo and Bill's argument, becoming aware of Margo's hostility.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve slip in quietly and catch the tail end of my argument with Bill, and I could tell she sensed my hostility right away.

grounded_facts: Eve looks to Margo before accepting a Martini, showing awareness of hierarchy.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Eve hesitated and looked to me before accepting a Martini, as if checking she had my permission, showing she knows her place.

grounded_facts: Margo repeatedly uses 'so many qualities' sarcastically to belittle Eve's praised attributes.
memories.memory_text: I kept saying 'so many qualities' to mock how everyone kept praising Eve, because it felt like they were using her supposed virtues to chip away at me.

grounded_facts: After downing a drink, Margo delivers a dramatic warning that the night will be turbulent, signaling emotional collapse and defiance.
memories.memory_text: I downed my drink and told everyone to fasten their seat belts because I knew it was going to be a bumpy night.

grounded_facts: A social gathering at Margo's home before a larger party, involving close friends and associates preparing for the evening's events.
memories.memory_text: I remember the small gathering at my place before the big party, where I downed drinks and watched people move through my home like I was losing control of everything.

grounded_facts: Margo commands the pianist to replay 'Liebestraum' despite his reluctance, asserting her control over the party's atmosphere.
memories.memory_text: I told the pianist to play 'Liebestraum' again, even though he didn't want to—I reminded him I was paying him and it was my piano, and if anyone didn't like the mood, they could leave.

grounded_facts: A post-gala gathering at Margo's home that has devolved into a somber, sparsely attended event marked by emotional tension and isolation.
memories.memory_text: I remember the post-gala gathering at my place feeling so somber and empty, with only a few people left, and me sitting there staring into my martini, just wanting the mood to stay as it was.

grounded_facts: Margo metaphorically declares that she is already dead, referring to herself as 'the remains of Margo Channing' sitting upright.
memories.memory_text: I told Bill that he was looking at the remains of Margo Channing, sitting up, because I feel like I'm already dead.

grounded_facts: When Bill relays guests' desire for happier music, Margo sarcastically suggests they go to the nursery.
memories.memory_text: When Bill whispered that the guests wanted happier music, I told him they should go to the nursery if they didn't like it here.

memories.memory_text: I told Max I’d put his name on the bicarbonate of soda box in the pantry, just for him, so it’ll always be there for Max Fabian.

grounded_facts: Margo explicitly tells Max she loves him, repeating it for emphasis, before inviting him to the pantry.
memories.memory_text: I told Max I love him, and I meant it—I said it twice so he’d know it’s true—then I invited him to come to the pantry with me.

grounded_facts: Margo finds and hands bicarb to Max for his indigestion, which he uses immediately.
memories.memory_text: I handed Max the bicarb for his indigestion, and I told him one good burp would help him feel better.

grounded_facts: Despite her doubts, Margo decides to accept the role of Cora in Lloyd's play.
memories.memory_text: Despite my doubts, I told Lloyd I would play his play, even if it meant wearing rompers and rolling in on a hoop.

grounded_facts: A private conversation among Margo, Max, and later Lloyd in the pantry after a party, discussing personal and professional matters.
memories.memory_text: I remember talking with Max and Lloyd in the pantry after the party, where I told Max that Miss Caswell could help him with scripts and interviews, and later I walked with Lloyd toward the stairs after agreeing to do his play.

grounded_facts: Eve speaks to a group about the emotional reward of being loved nightly by audiences.
memories.memory_text: I overheard Eve talking to a group about how it feels to be loved by audiences every night—their smiles, their shining eyes—and how anything is worth that.

grounded_facts: Margo exits a cab in front of the theater and enters the building on a Friday afternoon when there is no performance.
memories.memory_text: I got out of a cab in front of the theater and went inside on a Friday afternoon when there was no performance scheduled.

memories.memory_text: I arrived at the theater planning to read with Miss Caswell, but I saw for myself that it was nearly four o'clock, and the audition had already ended.

grounded_facts: Eve Harrington has been appointed as Margo's new understudy, replacing the previous pregnant understudy, marking a significant shift in casting dynamics.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Eve Harrington has been appointed as my new understudy, replacing the previous one who was pregnant, which came as a surprise.

grounded_facts: Miss Caswell's audition performance was so unremarkable or inadequate that Addison and others cannot recall it, suggesting it had no impact.
memories.memory_text: I wondered how bad Miss Caswell's performance must have been if no one, not even Addison, could remember it—maybe it meant it didn't leave any impression at all.

memories.memory_text: I was told the audition was set for 2:30 PM, and that Eve Harrington had performed with Miss Caswell, and Addison said her reading was something extraordinary, like a revelation.

memories.memory_text: I witnessed Addison tell me that Eve Harrington is now my understudy, and he spoke about her with such reverence, comparing her to legendary actresses, as if he'd had a revelation.

memories.memory_text: I felt the weight of Addison's words when he exalted Eve's performance in front of me, knowing he was drawing a line between her rising brilliance and my place in the theater.

memories.memory_text: I listened as Addison described Eve's reading not as reading but as a brilliant performance, something made of music and fire, comparing her to legends like Jeanne Eagels.

memories.memory_text: I saw Addison tell Miss Caswell that her next move should be toward television, effectively closing the door on her chances here at the theater.

memories.memory_text: I arrived late to the theater, marching down the aisle and apologizing for missing the start, not knowing the audition had already happened.

grounded_facts: An audition was held for the role, featuring Eve and Miss Caswell, which concluded before Margo arrived.
memories.memory_text: I realized an audition must have taken place while I was gone, with Eve and Miss Caswell, and that Eve had performed so well they called her a revelation.

grounded_facts: Lloyd blames Margo for turning a minor misunderstanding into a major confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I heard Lloyd say I had a genius for turning an innocent misunderstanding into a barroom brawl, and it only made me angrier because he refused to see how deeply I'd been wronged.

grounded_facts: Margo accuses Lloyd of favoring Eve and distorting the creative process, leading to a heated argument.
memories.memory_text: I accused Lloyd of favoring Eve and distorting the creative process, and when he said I turned a misunderstanding into a brawl, I fired back that I was being lied to and attacked behind my back.

grounded_facts: Margo and Max engage in a public argument about her contract and potential breach, raising legal implications.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Max about my contract and whether he was threatening legal action, standing my ground even when he played the victim by saying he was a dying man.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Margo, in a moment of vulnerability, asks Bill if he is leaving to find Eve, revealing her deep-seated insecurity.

memories.memory_text: I told Karen about Eve, praising her as a born actress with everything a playwright could dream of, and contrasted her with Margo, implying Margo's self-centeredness was a problem.

memories.memory_text: I came home furious after the audition and vented to Karen about Margo's unprofessional behavior, saying she was hysterical and deserved a boot in the rear.

memories.memory_text: Karen told me about a weekend trip to the country that the four of us—her, Lloyd, Bill, and me—were planning to take.

grounded_facts: Karen calls Eve's residence, requesting to speak with her, marking the first direct action in her plan.
memories.memory_text: I picked up the phone by Lloyd's chair, looked in the leather phone book, dialed, and asked to speak with Eve Harrington, marking the first step in my plan.

grounded_facts: A journey in a car to deliver Margo to the train station in time for her theater performance.
memories.memory_text: I remember we were on our way to the train station so I wouldn't miss my performance, and someone said we'd arrive with plenty of time.

grounded_facts: The car stops functioning due to an empty fuel tank, stranding the group on a remote road.
memories.memory_text: I heard the car make that hissing sound when it runs out of gas, and I remember thinking it couldn't be true—how could we be stranded like this?

grounded_facts: Karen takes responsibility for not checking the fuel level earlier, expressing deep regret for the group's predicament.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Karen regretted not checking the fuel level and felt responsible for us being stranded.

grounded_facts: Karen expresses deep regret for not checking the fuel level, taking blame for the group's predicament.
memories.memory_text: I heard Karen admit she didn't check the fuel, and I could tell she felt bad about it, taking the blame for us being stuck.

grounded_facts: Lloyd chooses to leave the car and walk half a mile to seek assistance or gas.

grounded_facts: Margo admits she has not been pleasant lately and sincerely apologizes to Karen.
Margo acknowledges her unpleasant demeanor over recent weeks and expresses sincere regret to Karen.
memories.memory_text: I admitted to Karen that I haven't been very pleasant lately and apologized sincerely, because I truly regret how I've been acting.

grounded_facts: Margo shares her fear that Bill loves her persona, not her true self, and expresses anxiety about aging and authenticity.
Margo confesses her fear that Bill loves her stage persona, not her true self, and expresses anxiety about aging and womanhood.
memories.memory_text: I shared with Karen my fear that Bill loves Margo Channing, not the real me, and confessed how uncertain I feel about who I am without the persona—especially as I face aging and what it means to be a woman beyond the stage.

grounded_facts: The group is immobilized in a car after it runs out of gas, leading to intimate conversation and emotional revelations.
memories.memory_text: I remember how, after the car stalled, we were all stuck there together and I ended up speaking honestly about feeling insecure and unloved, like an infant throwing a tantrum, and how being a woman means more than just a career.

grounded_facts: Bill states he is in love with Margo and does not want Eve pursuing him romantically.
memories.memory_text: I overheard that Bill is in love with me and doesn't want Eve pursuing him, though I wasn't there when he said it.

grounded_facts: Karen exits a taxi and enters the '21' Club in New York.
memories.memory_text: I remember Karen arriving for our lunch at '21'—she must have exited a taxi and walked into the club, though I didn't see it directly.

memories.memory_text: I read aloud from Addison's column, my hands shaking as I saw how it mocked mature actresses and hinted at Eve's words, feeling the sting of its veiled attack.

grounded_facts: A gathering in Margo's living room where she reacts to a damaging newspaper column attributed to Eve Harrington's statements.
memories.memory_text: I was in my living room with Karen when I read the column, and I couldn't help but react to that outdated phrase—something I thought had gone out with Woollcott.

grounded_facts: Margo verbally attacks Eve and Addison deWitt, blaming them for the damaging column and threatening retaliation.
memories.memory_text: I verbally attacked Eve and Addison deWitt, threatening to make them pay for the damage they've done, saying I'd personally stuff that pathetic little lost lamb down deWitt's throat if no one else would act.

grounded_facts: Margo expresses fury and disbelief over the content of the column, interpreting it as a personal attack orchestrated by Eve and Addison deWitt.
memories.memory_text: I felt furious and betrayed, crumpling the paper in my hands and lashing out, blaming Eve and Addison deWitt for orchestrating this attack, vowing I'd make them pay if no one else would stop them.

grounded_facts: Bill physically embraces Margo and reassures her after her emotional breakdown upon reading the column.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Bill physically embraces Margo and reassures her after her emotional breakdown upon reading the column.

grounded_facts: Bill enters the room after reading the column and comforts Margo, who breaks down in his arms.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Bill enters the room after reading the column and comforts Margo, who breaks down in his arms.

grounded_facts: Karen recognizes her presence is superfluous in the intimate moment between Bill and Margo and leaves the room.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Karen recognizes her presence is superfluous in the intimate moment between Bill and Margo and leaves the room.

grounded_facts: Lloyd informs Karen that Eve visited him and tried to explain her interview, but broke down crying.
memories.memory_text: I heard from Lloyd that Eve visited him to explain her interview and tried to apologize, but she broke down crying and couldn't finish.

grounded_facts: Lloyd reveals he has considered casting Eve Harrington in the lead role of 'Footsteps on the Ceiling,' inspired during Eve's visit, though he acknowledges practical difficulties.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Lloyd got the idea to cast Eve in 'Footsteps on the Ceiling' while she was talking to him, though there are practical issues with making it happen.

grounded_facts: Karen angrily opposes Lloyd's suggestion to cast Eve as Cora, accusing him of moral weakness and disloyalty to Margo.
Karen vehemently rejects the idea of Eve playing Cora, interpreting it as a betrayal of Margo and a sign of moral decay.
memories.memory_text: I saw Karen fiercely reject the idea of Eve playing Cora, calling it a betrayal of me and a sign of moral decay, and I heard her tell Lloyd not to even consider giving Eve the part.

grounded_facts: Margo calls to invite Lloyd and Karen to meet her and Bill at the Cub Room after the theater, restoring emotional calm after the argument.
memories.memory_text: I called Lloyd and Karen to invite them to meet Bill and me at the Cub Room after the theater for a bottle of wine, hoping it would help restore calm after the argument.

grounded_facts: A post-theater social meeting planned at the Cub Room involving Margo, Bill, Lloyd, and Karen.
memories.memory_text: I remember suggesting to Bill that we invite Lloyd and Karen to meet us at the Cub Room after the show for a bottle of wine.

grounded_facts: Lloyd clarifies that he did not promise Eve the role and cited Karen's opposition as a key reason.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Lloyd that he didn’t promise Eve anything and that he cited my clear preference for playing the role as a key reason he wouldn’t make any change without my approval.

grounded_facts: A celebratory dinner among Margo, Bill, Lloyd, and Karen at the Stork Club, marked by wine, toasts, and engagement announcements.
memories.memory_text: I was at a celebratory dinner with Bill, Lloyd, and Karen at the Stork Club, where we shared wine and toasts, feeling happy and relaxed together.

grounded_facts: Bill publicly declares Margo as his bride-to-be during a toast, shifting the tone from celebration to engagement announcement.
Bill interrupts Lloyd to sincerely propose a heartfelt toast to Margo, declaring her as his bride-to-be.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill interrupting Lloyd to give a heartfelt toast, declaring me as his bride-to-be and saying we’d meet at City Hall the next morning, looking right at me when he said it.

grounded_facts: Margo and Bill reveal their intention to get married the next day at City Hall, with a three-day waiting period due to legal requirements.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill toasting me as his bride-to-be and telling me we’d meet at City Hall the next day to get married, with a three-day waiting period required by law, and I told him I’d be on time.

grounded_facts: Lloyd makes a sarcastic comment about the note being from Karen's lover, introducing tension and discomfort.
memories.memory_text: I heard Lloyd make a sarcastic comment about a midnight elopement, and it felt like he was mocking the idea of a real commitment, which added to the tension at the table.

grounded_facts: Eve sends a discreet note to Karen requesting an urgent meeting in the Ladies' Room, interrupting the celebration.
memories.memory_text: I saw a waiter deliver a note to Karen, and I knew it was from Eve asking for an urgent meeting in the Ladies' Room, which interrupted our celebration.

grounded_facts: Margo reads Eve's urgent note to the group, revealing Eve's desire to speak with Karen privately.
memories.memory_text: I read Eve's note out loud to the group, saying she needed to speak with Karen privately and underlined 'meet me in the Ladies' Room,' which made me curious about what she wanted.

grounded_facts: Margo breaks her long-standing habit of accompanying Karen to the Ladies' Room, choosing instead to stay behind out of curiosity about Eve.
memories.memory_text: I told Karen that in all our years of friendship, I'd never let her go to the Ladies' Room alone—but this time, I had to stay behind because I was dying to know what was going on in that feverish little brain of Eve's.

grounded_facts: Addison rises and politely greets Karen as she passes, but she ignores him completely.
memories.memory_text: I saw Karen get up and walk past Addison, who rose to greet her, but she ignored him completely and didn't say a word.

grounded_facts: Eve directly asks Karen to recommend her to Lloyd for the role of 'Cora', framing it as something only Karen can do.
memories.memory_text: I heard Eve press Karen directly, saying 'Cora' was her part and that Karen had to tell Lloyd to give it to her, as if it were something only Karen could do.

grounded_facts: Eve reveals she knows how she got the chance to replace Margo and threatens to expose Karen's complicity unless Karen recommends her for the role of 'Cora'.
memories.memory_text: I overheard Eve coldly tell Karen that she knew how I missed that performance and how she got the chance to replace me, and that she’d keep it quiet only if Karen supported her for the role of 'Cora'.

grounded_facts: Karen expresses disbelief and moral judgment at Eve's willingness to destroy relationships for a role.
memories.memory_text: I remember Karen expressing disbelief, saying Eve would do all that just for a part in a play, as if she couldn’t believe someone would destroy relationships for a role.

grounded_facts: A celebratory post-wedding gathering at the Cub Room where the group drinks champagne and reflects on recent events.
memories.memory_text: I remember the celebratory gathering at the Cub Room, where we all drank champagne and I felt especially cheery, surrounded by the group as Karen joined us.

grounded_facts: Margo publicly declares she forgives Eve, acknowledging Eve's role in bringing the group together, despite earlier hostility.
Margo acknowledges that the current happiness of the group is indirectly due to Eve's actions, despite calling her 'Little Miss Evil'.
memories.memory_text: I publicly forgave Eve that night, even called her 'Little Miss Evil,' but I meant it when I said I forgive her — because the four of us being together like that, it was her doing, and that’s something good I didn’t expect.

grounded_facts: Margo tells Bill she will be a 'married lady' with a real home and life, marking a shift from her previous identity.
memories.memory_text: I told Bill I was going to be a married lady with a real home and a life that meant something, not just a house I was afraid to stay in alone.

grounded_facts: Margo declares she no longer wants to play the role of Cora, citing her new married life and desire to move beyond acting roles that no longer fit her identity.
memories.memory_text: I told Lloyd I didn't want to play Cora anymore because I finally have a life to live, and I don't need to pretend in roles that don't fit me just to fill my nights.

grounded_facts: After Margo rejects the role of Cora, Karen suddenly bursts into uncontrollable laughter, masking her inner turmoil and guilt.
memories.memory_text: After I said I wouldn't play Cora, Karen suddenly burst into hysterical laughter, and I could see she was struggling beneath it.

grounded_facts: Addison declares that Eve belongs to him, citing their shared traits of ambition, contempt for humanity, and emotional incapacity, establishing a twisted bond of mutual recognition.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Addison declares that Eve belongs to him, citing their shared traits of ambition, contempt for humanity, and emotional incapacity, establishing a twisted bond of mutual recognition.

memories.memory_text: I heard Eve thank Max Fabian for taking a chance on her as an unknown actress during her speech.

grounded_facts: Eve thanks Karen as her first friend in the theater.
memories.memory_text: I remember Eve thanking Karen as her first friend in the theater, mentioning her kindness and graciousness.

grounded_facts: Eve honors Margo Channing as her idol and future benefactor.
memories.memory_text: I was acknowledged by Eve as her idol and future benefactor, a moment that stood out even though I remained skeptical of her sincerity.

grounded_facts: Eve thanks Bill Sampson for his demanding yet patient direction.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Eve thank Bill Sampson for his demanding yet patient direction during her speech.

grounded_facts: Eve acknowledges Lloyd Richards for writing the play and believing in her.
memories.memory_text: I saw Eve acknowledge Lloyd Richards for writing the play and believing in her, asking how she could ever repay him.

grounded_facts: Eve reveals her upcoming move to Hollywood to make a film, while affirming her emotional commitment to the theater.
memories.memory_text: I heard Eve announce she’s going to Hollywood to make a film, though she claimed her heart would always remain in the theater.

memories.memory_text: I saw Karen offer a brief, formal 'Congratulations, Eve' as she was leaving, and Eve politely thanked her.

memories.memory_text: I delivered a sharp remark to Eve after her speech, telling her not to worry about her heart because she could always put that award where her heart ought to be.
