grounded_facts: Addison deWitt identifies Max Fabian as a theatrical producer driven by financial risk rather than art.
memories.memory_text: I heard Addison deWitt describe Max Fabian as a producer focused on financial risk, someone out to make a buck from each production.

grounded_facts: It is disclosed that the role for which Eve Harrington won the award was originally meant for Margo Channing.
memories.memory_text: I was told during the ceremony that the role I won the Sarah Siddons Award for was originally meant for Margo Channing.

grounded_facts: Addison deWitt presents Margo Channing as a legendary theater star whose role was given to Eve Harrington.
memories.memory_text: I learned that Margo Channing was a legendary star and that the role I received the Sarah Siddons Award for was originally meant for her.

grounded_facts: The aged actor delivers a ceremonial speech extolling Eve Harrington's youth, humility, and devotion to theater.
memories.memory_text: I remember the aged actor speaking so warmly about me—my youth, my humility, and how my heart is as old as the theater itself—while he held the Sarah Siddons Award, calling it the highest honor in the theater and saying my dream had come true.

grounded_facts: Eve Harrington is formally presented with the Sarah Siddons Award for Distinguished Achievement in a public ceremony, with the action pausing at the moment of award transfer as sound and motion stop.
memories.memory_text: I stood and received a standing ovation, then walked toward the aged actor as the applause continued and flashbulbs went off; I reached out and took the Sarah Siddons Award from him, feeling the weight of it in my hands as everything seemed to pause in that moment.

grounded_facts: An impromptu encounter between Karen and Eve in the alley outside the theater, where Eve is discovered waiting in secret admiration.
memories.memory_text: I was waiting in the alley outside the theater, hoping Karen wouldn't mind me speaking to her, and I finally gathered the courage to say something when she noticed me.

grounded_facts: Karen decides to bring Eve to meet Margo Channing after learning about her devotion as a fan.
memories.memory_text: I was told Karen is going to take me to meet Margo Channing because she believes Margo has to meet me after hearing how devoted I am as a fan.

grounded_facts: Eve expresses insecurity about meeting Margo in her current appearance, and Karen reassures her that she looks fine.
memories.memory_text: I felt unsure about meeting Margo looking the way I did, so I told Karen I might have come at a bad time, but she reassured me that I looked just fine.

grounded_facts: When asked, Eve introduces herself by name for the first time.
memories.memory_text: When Karen asked for my name, I introduced myself clearly: I said, 'Eve. Eve Harrington.'

grounded_facts: Eve arrives at the backstage of Curran Theater, experiencing a sense of awe and reverence upon entering.
memories.memory_text: I entered the backstage of the Curran Theater like a novitiate stepping into the Vatican, overwhelmed with awe and reverence.

grounded_facts: Eve verbalizes her sense of wonder about the backstage atmosphere, inviting Karen's共鸣.
memories.memory_text: I said to Karen, 'You can breathe it—can't you? Like some magic perfume,' sharing my wonder about the backstage atmosphere.

grounded_facts: Karen gently takes Eve's arm, signaling guidance and companionship.
Karen leads Eve toward Margo's stage dressing room in the Curran Theater backstage during the evening.
Karen acknowledges the doorman with a polite greeting as they pass.
memories.memory_text: I saw Karen greet the doorman with a polite 'Good evening, Gus,' and then she gently took my arm, leading me toward Margo's dressing room.

grounded_facts: Eve, accompanied by Karen, arrives at Margo's dressing room door, waiting briefly before entering as Margo speaks from inside.
An informal moment in Margo's dressing room where she speaks loudly from within, engaging someone inside while Karen and Eve arrive outside.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at Margo's dressing room with Karen, and we paused outside when I heard Margo laughing loudly from inside, clearly in the middle of a lively moment.

grounded_facts: Karen whispers to Eve to wait a moment before entering, indicating caution or timing.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Karen to wait a moment before going in, so I stayed back as she whispered to me not to rush in.

grounded_facts: Margo delivers a loud, humorous line from inside the dressing room, referencing a hypothetical Southern victory in the Civil War.
memories.memory_text: I heard Margo call out loudly from inside her dressing room, joking that if the South had won the war, someone could write the same plays about the North.

grounded_facts: Karen reveals that Eve Harrington, a devoted fan, is waiting outside Margo's dressing room and insists Margo see her.
Karen insists that Margo meet Eve, emphasizing Eve's devotion and emotional investment.
memories.memory_text: I remember Karen telling Margo that I was waiting outside her dressing room and insisting she see me, saying I worshipped her and that I was her whole life.

grounded_facts: A private gathering in Margo's dressing room after a performance, involving close associates and a visiting fan.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Karen brought me into Margo's dressing room after the show, and she introduced me to Margo and the others as Eve Harrington.

grounded_facts: Margo uses quiet menace to send Birdie back to the bathroom to avoid disruption during Eve's introduction.
memories.memory_text: I saw Margo quietly tell Birdie to go back to the bathroom with a sharp whisper, and I noticed how everyone tensed when she came out, realizing she had interrupted something important.

grounded_facts: Eve tells Margo she has attended every performance and that seeing her is the only meaningful activity in her life.
memories.memory_text: I told Margo that attending every one of her performances was the only meaningful thing in my life, that seeing her act filled me in a way nothing else ever has.

grounded_facts: Eve recounts her isolated upbringing in Wisconsin and the death of her husband Eddie in the war, explaining how attending Margo's performance of 'Remembrance' in San Francisco became a turning point, forging her deep emotional attachment to Margo.
memories.memory_text: I remember telling them about growing up alone in Wisconsin, how make-believe felt more real than real life, and how I left the farm to work as a secretary in a brewery just to help my family. I shared how hard it was after Eddie died in the war — I stayed in San Francisco because I couldn’t go back without him, and how seeing Margo’s performance of 'Remembrance' changed everything. I told them I went to every show, and when the play moved East, I followed — because that night in the theater was the most important moment of my life, until the one I was living right then.

grounded_facts: After mocking Eve's story, Birdie sincerely apologizes, acknowledging her bluntness and showing unexpected respect.
memories.memory_text: I remember Birdie apologizing to me after mocking my story, saying she was sorry if she hurt my feelings and that it was just her way of talking, and when I told her she hadn't, she invited me to call her Birdie, which felt like a small but sincere gesture of respect.

grounded_facts: Bill briefly acknowledges Eve only after being reminded by Karen, showing little interest or respect.
memories.memory_text: Bill barely acknowledged me at first, and only after Karen reminded him did he ask my name, saying 'Hello, what's your name?' as if I were a stranger he'd just noticed.

grounded_facts: Bill Sampson enters Margo's dressing room unannounced, disrupting the gathering with his energetic and chaotic presence, revealing he is about to leave for a film shoot.
memories.memory_text: I was still absorbing Margo's kindness when the door burst open and Bill Sampson stormed in, dropping his suitcase and filling the room with his loud energy, clearly on his way to a film shoot.

grounded_facts: Margo impulsively decides to delay her departure with Bill to spend time alone with Eve after the others leave.
Margo insists Eve stay after others leave, signaling a shift from skepticism to personal investment in their connection.
memories.memory_text: I remember Margo telling me to stick around after the others left, asking me to go somewhere and talk just the two of us—she even put off her plans with Bill for it. I could tell she really wanted me to stay, and that meant something to me.

grounded_facts: Karen tells Eve she hopes to see her again not just as a fan, but as a friend, extending personal warmth.
memories.memory_text: I remember Karen telling me she hoped to see me again not just as a fan, but as a friend, and it made me feel truly seen.

grounded_facts: Eve tells Karen she will never forget the night or her role in making it possible, emphasizing emotional significance.
memories.memory_text: I told Karen I'd never forget that night or her for making it possible, and I meant every word—I carry that moment with me.

grounded_facts: Bill explains his philosophical view of theater, justifying his decision to go to Hollywood as an expansion of theatrical art beyond traditional boundaries.
memories.memory_text: I listened to Bill explain that theater isn't just in New York or London—that it's anywhere there's magic and make-believe, even in Hollywood—and that it's for everybody, whether I like it or not.

grounded_facts: Bill tells Margo to throw away a letter she's been carrying, calling it dreary and boring.
memories.memory_text: I was present when Bill told Margo to throw away that letter, saying it was dreary and bored him.

grounded_facts: Eve persistently questions Bill's motivation for going to Hollywood, implying disapproval or concern.
memories.memory_text: I questioned Bill about why he had to go to Hollywood, watching him closely the whole time, and I told him he mustn't stay there.

grounded_facts: Margo cannot find her second earring while preparing to leave.
memories.memory_text: I saw Margo fumbling with her ear and saying she couldn't find her other earring while we were getting ready to leave.

grounded_facts: Margo finds and then throws away a letter she has been carrying, prompted by Bill's comment.
memories.memory_text: I saw Margo find the letter she'd been carrying and then throw it away after Bill made his remark.

grounded_facts: Bill embraces Birdie and kisses her cheek before leaving; she returns the kiss.
Birdie tells Bill to 'kill the people' as a way of wishing him success at the event.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill embrace Birdie and kiss her cheek before leaving, and she kissed him back; then she told him to 'kill the people' as a way of wishing him luck.

grounded_facts: Margo and Eve leave the dressing room ahead of Bill, marking the end of preparation and transition to the awards event.
memories.memory_text: Margo and I left the dressing room ahead of Bill, marking the end of our preparations and the start of the awards event.

grounded_facts: Margo, Eve, Bill, and Birdie gather in Margo's dressing room as she finishes getting ready to attend a public event.
memories.memory_text: I was in Margo's dressing room with her, Bill, and Birdie while she finished getting ready for the event, and I left right after her, just ahead of Bill.

grounded_facts: A logistical and emotional moment at LaGuardia Field where Margo, Bill, and Eve prepare for Bill's flight departure.
memories.memory_text: I was at LaGuardia Field with Margo and Bill, watching them cling to each other as they faced his impending departure, and I could feel how every passing moment tightened the pressure around us.

grounded_facts: Eve proposes to take care of the check-in procedures so Margo and Bill can spend their last moments together before departure.
Eve verbally proposes to manage the check-in so Margo and Bill can have private time before Bill's departure.
memories.memory_text: I offered to handle the check-in procedures so Margo and Bill could have some private time before he left, and I told them I could meet them at the gate with the ticket.

grounded_facts: Bill gives the airplane ticket to Eve, authorizing her to complete the check-in process.
memories.memory_text: I took the airplane ticket from Bill, feeling the weight of being trusted to handle the check-in for everyone.

grounded_facts: Margo smiles gratefully at Eve after she accepts the task of handling check-in.
memories.memory_text: I saw Margo smile at me with genuine gratitude after I accepted the task, and I smiled back, knowing I was helping her through a tender moment.

grounded_facts: Bill stops kissing Margo upon noticing Eve standing near them with his ticket.
memories.memory_text: I stood near Bill and Margo, and I saw him stop kissing her when he noticed me with his ticket.

grounded_facts: Eve hands Bill his ticket, indicating readiness to proceed toward the gate.
memories.memory_text: I handed Bill his ticket to let him know we were ready to go toward the gate.

grounded_facts: A moment at LaGuardia airport where Bill and Margo are preparing to leave, interrupted by Eve's arrival with the ticket.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at LaGuardia just in time to see Bill and Margo about to kiss, and I held out his ticket before they noticed me; then I handed it to him and we started toward the gate.

grounded_facts: Bill asks Eve to look after Margo in his absence, framing her as someone who needs companionship.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Bill to keep an eye on Margo and not let her get lonely, like she's a loose lamb in a jungle.

grounded_facts: A farewell gathering at the boarding gate as Bill departs on a flight.
Bill boards the plane after saying goodbye to Margo and Eve, marking his physical departure from the scene.
memories.memory_text: I stood with Margo at the boarding gate as Bill said his goodbyes, held her when she turned away, and watched him pause, wave, and finally board the plane while I stayed close to her, ready to comfort her as we walked away together.

grounded_facts: After Bill leaves, Eve shifts from linking arms to placing her arm comfortingly around Margo as they walk.
memories.memory_text: After Bill left, I shifted from linking arms with Margo to putting my arm comfortingly around her as we walked away.

grounded_facts: Addison offers Margo a drink; she declines absently, indicating preoccupation with her thoughts about Eve.
memories.memory_text: I was lost in thought about Eve when Addison offered me a drink, but I didn't want it and just shook my head, still thinking of her.

grounded_facts: Eve brings letters for Margo to sign and exchanges them for the script Margo returns.
memories.memory_text: I brought the letters for Margo to sign and handed them to her, then took the script she returned with a smile.

grounded_facts: Eve intercepts the phone call and skillfully rejects the caller, demonstrating control over access to Margo.
memories.memory_text: I reached for the phone before Birdie could get to it, and I politely but firmly turned the caller away because I knew they weren't worth Margo's time.

grounded_facts: Birdie glares at Eve after she intercepts the phone call, showing resentment toward Eve's growing influence.
memories.memory_text: I saw Birdie glare at me after I took the call, and I could feel her resentment building toward me.

grounded_facts: Birdie slams the door as she leaves after being overridden by Eve in answering the phone.
memories.memory_text: I saw Birdie slam the door as she left after I answered the phone and overruled her.

grounded_facts: Post-performance audience acknowledgment where Margo receives repeated applause.
memories.memory_text: I stood there watching and listening to the storm of applause, feeling my heart race as the audience roared for Margo.

grounded_facts: Margo decides not to take another curtain call, signaling a shift in her relationship with audience validation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Margo shake her head and say she wouldn't take another curtain call, that from now on it was just something to do until the aisles cleared.

grounded_facts: Eve tells Margo she could watch her perform the final scene a thousand times and cry each time.
Eve tells Margo she is profoundly moved by her performance, revealing emotional investment and reverence.
memories.memory_text: I told Margo I could watch her play that final scene a thousand times and still cry every time, because her performance truly moved me.

grounded_facts: Margo responds to Eve's praise with self-deprecating humor about performing a thousand times.
memories.memory_text: I heard Margo respond with a grin, saying her thousandth performance would happen in a well-padded booby hatch if she lasted that long.

grounded_facts: Margo and Eve transition from the stage area to Margo's dressing room, initiating a private post-show interaction.
memories.memory_text: I walked with Margo from the stage toward her dressing room, continuing to talk about the performance and how things have changed from the original staging.

grounded_facts: Eve points out deviations in staging since the director's absence, showing attention to detail and alignment with Margo's standards.
Eve expresses disapproval of how the cast has altered the production in the director's absence.
memories.memory_text: I told Margo how disgraceful it was that the cast kept changing everything in the play since the director's been away, because I really care about keeping the performance true to how it should be.

grounded_facts: Eve informs Margo about a specific deviation in Roger Ferraday's stage positioning during her scene with her father.
Eve informs Margo that Roger Ferraday has been moving closer during her second-act scene.
memories.memory_text: I pointed out to Margo that Roger Ferraday has been moving closer during her second-act scene with her father, even though he's supposed to stay upstage at the arch, because I noticed it was happening every night.

grounded_facts: Eve helps Margo unhook her gown, indicating intimacy and service.
Margo allows Eve to help her unhook her gown as they enter the dressing room.
memories.memory_text: I helped Margo unhook her gown as we entered the dressing room, and she allowed me to do it, letting me be close in that moment of intimacy and service.

grounded_facts: Margo jokingly threatens to spit in Roger Ferraday's eye if he continues moving closer during the scene.
Margo jokes that she will spit in Roger Ferraday's eye if he comes too close.
memories.memory_text: I heard Margo joke that she'd spit in Roger Ferraday's eye if he got too close during the scene, and it made me feel like she was taking back control.

grounded_facts: Eve takes initiative to return Margo's costume to the wardrobe mistress, overstepping her role.
memories.memory_text: I took Margo's costume to return it to the wardrobe mistress while she was cleaning up, and I left the room with it.

grounded_facts: Birdie indirectly alerts Margo that Eve is violating backstage norms by handling costume duties, implying potential trouble.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Birdie that the wardrobe women are very touchy, and that handling their duties could cause trouble.

grounded_facts: Margo understands from Birdie's comment that Eve is encroaching on the duties of the unionized wardrobe mistress, which could cause conflict.
memories.memory_text: I realized Eve was taking over the costume duties that belong to the unionized wardrobe mistress, and I understood that this could create conflict, so I rushed out after her.

grounded_facts: A private moment in Margo's dressing room after her stage performance, involving informal interaction with Birdie and Eve.
memories.memory_text: I was in Margo's dressing room after her performance, sitting by her discarded costume while she changed, and Birdie made a joke about the room needing a basketball hoop.

grounded_facts: Eve holds Margo's dress against her body and mimics Margo's performance gestures in front of mirrors, indicating identification with or aspiration to Margo's role.
memories.memory_text: I held Margo's dress against my body and mimicked her performance gestures in front of the mirrors, bowing as if to applause, trying to see myself as her.

grounded_facts: Margo stops Eve from continuing to wear or handle her dress by instructing that wardrobe should be handled by Mrs. Brown.
Margo quietly but firmly directs Eve to stop handling her costume, signaling disapproval and boundary-setting.
memories.memory_text: I was startled when Margo quietly said we should let Mrs. Brown handle the wardrobe, and I knew she meant I had to stop touching her dress, so I wordlessly brought it back.

grounded_facts: Bill mentions that Eve has been writing to him weekly and organizing his return party, indicating her increasing presence in his life during his absence.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill telling me that Eve has been writing to him every week and organizing his return party, and that he even sent her a list of people to invite.

grounded_facts: When Bill asks about Eve, Margo responds with minimal engagement and deflects by saying she will 'check with Eve,' implying Eve now manages their shared social arrangements.
memories.memory_text: When Bill asked about Eve, I saw Margo give a short answer and then say she’d check with Eve, as if Eve is now the one handling their plans.

grounded_facts: Eve admits she forgot to inform Margo about arranging a birthday message to Bill, but took initiative to send a telegram herself.
Eve reveals she sent a birthday telegram to Bill on Margo's behalf without informing her.
memories.memory_text: I admitted I forgot to tell Margo, but I went ahead and sent the birthday telegram to Bill because I knew she’d want to do it and she’s been so busy.

grounded_facts: A domestic morning scene where Margo receives breakfast and engages in conversations with Birdie and Eve.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at Margo's with my new suit on and showed it off, joking about how she might want it altered for herself, and though she made a comment about me always being one step ahead, I nearly forgot to tell her I'd sent Bill a birthday telegram—then realized it when I was already leaving, and she seemed to appreciate it.

grounded_facts: After Eve's revelation, Margo silently reflects, showing signs of growing distrust toward Eve's expanding role in her life.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Margo staring quietly after I left, and she seemed lost in thought, twirling her orange juice like something was bothering her.

grounded_facts: Margo silently toasts Karen by raising her glass, creating a moment of mutual recognition.
memories.memory_text: I saw Margo raise her glass in a silent toast, and in that moment, we both seemed to understand something unspoken.

grounded_facts: Karen reflects on her past encounters with Eve, noting they did not speak meaningfully until a later party.
memories.memory_text: I remember being told that Eve and I didn’t really talk meaningfully until the party Margo gave for Bill after he came back from Hollywood, even though I’d seen her often before that.

grounded_facts: Karen reassures Eve that she is not a charity case and acknowledges her significant contributions to Margo's well-being.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Karen that I'm not a charity case and that I've truly helped Margo, which made me feel recognized for my efforts.

grounded_facts: Eve hesitantly asks Karen to speak to Mr. Fabian about appointing her as Margo's understudy.
Eve expresses her desire to become Margo's new understudy, citing her deep knowledge of the role and staging, and asks Karen to speak to Mr. Fabian about it.
memories.memory_text: I hesitantly asked Karen to speak to Mr. Fabian about making me Margo's understudy because I know the role so well and heard the current understudy was leaving, and I wanted to use my knowledge to contribute more.

grounded_facts: Eve hugs Karen in gratitude after securing her promise to advocate for the understudy position.
memories.memory_text: I hugged Karen in gratitude after she promised to talk to Mr. Fabian about the understudy position.

grounded_facts: An ongoing party at Margo's home late at night, subdued in tone, with guests downstairs while private conversations occur in the bedroom.
memories.memory_text: I remember being at Margo's late-night party, where the mood was subdued and guests were downstairs while Karen and I had our conversation in private upstairs.

grounded_facts: Eve speaks passionately about the value of applause and audience love, revealing her deep emotional investment in theatrical recognition.
memories.memory_text: I spoke up about how applause feels like waves of love from the audience, wrapping you up and making you feel like you belong—just that alone is worth any sacrifice.

grounded_facts: Margo sarcastically implies Eve would willingly perform intimate acts to serve her, rejecting Eve's offer with contempt.
memories.memory_text: I offered to help Margo when she said she was going to bed, and she mocked me by suggesting I’d take off her clothes or tuck her in like a servant—then made it clear she didn’t want me to, not even a little.

grounded_facts: Intoxicated and defensive, Margo mocks Eve's deference and abruptly ends the evening by going to bed, assigning Bill the role of host.
memories.memory_text: I saw Margo get increasingly bitter and drunk, and when she finally snapped, I watched her hand over hosting duties to Bill before walking out on all of us.

grounded_facts: After Margo's exit, Eve breaks down in tears and is consoled by Karen, who acknowledges Margo's difficult behavior without excusing it.
Karen physically and verbally reassures Eve after Margo's outburst, minimizing Eve's self-blame.
memories.memory_text: I broke down in tears after Margo left, and Karen came to me, put her arm around me, and told me not to mind Margo too much, even though she knows how difficult Margo can be — she even said she sometimes wants to kick her — and that helped me feel less alone.

grounded_facts: A late-night informal assembly of theater people on the stairs after a party, marked by intellectual banter, emotional tension, and eventual conflict.
memories.memory_text: I was there on the stairs with the others after the party, sitting among the theater people while they talked, and I noticed Margo's smile fade when I stood up; later, we all laughed and said good night before going downstairs.

grounded_facts: As the group disperses, Eve asks Karen not to forget their earlier conversation, and Karen assures her she won't.
Eve asks Karen not to forget their prior private conversation, seeking confirmation of ongoing support.
memories.memory_text: As we were leaving, I asked Karen if she would remember our earlier talk, and she promised she wouldn’t forget, which made me feel sure I still have her support.

grounded_facts: An informal moment of shared laughter and storytelling between Bill and Eve in the living room, interrupted by Margo's arrival.
memories.memory_text: I was laughing with Bill, completely caught up in his story, feeling the easy connection between us as he talked and I looked up at him.

grounded_facts: Bill shares an anecdote involving a cameraman and DeMille, causing Eve to chuckle.
memories.memory_text: I was listening to Bill tell a story about a cameraman and DeMille, and I couldn't help but chuckle at the punchline.

grounded_facts: Upon seeing Margo approach, Eve stops laughing, ends her engagement with Bill's story, and stands up.
Margo deliberately reaches the landing and begins moving toward the living room where Bill and Eve are conversing.
Margo's deliberate arrival and approach cause Eve to stop laughing and stand up, and Bill to turn around, ending the intimacy of the moment.
memories.memory_text: I saw Margo approaching on the landing, and I immediately stopped laughing, stood up, and broke off the moment with Bill as he turned around.

grounded_facts: Margo confronts Bill about his extended conversation with Eve, interpreting it as a sign of romantic interest and expressing jealousy masked as criticism of Eve's 'qualities'.
Margo implies that Bill is overly impressed by Eve's youth and supposed virtues, using sarcasm to express her insecurity.
memories.memory_text: I remember Margo confronting Bill, sarcastically listing my qualities like loyalty and youth, masking her jealousy as criticism while I was there.

grounded_facts: Bill rebukes Margo for judging Eve harshly, framing her behavior as innocent admiration and accusing Margo of insecurity.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Bill rebuked Margo for judging me harshly, defending me by saying my admiration was innocent and that her accusations came from insecurity.

grounded_facts: When offered a drink by Bill, Eve looks to Margo for approval, acknowledging her as the authority figure.
memories.memory_text: I looked to Margo when Bill offered me a drink, waiting for her approval before saying what I wanted, because she was the one in charge.

grounded_facts: After downing her drink, Margo delivers a dramatic line signaling the beginning of a turbulent evening, marking a shift in tone.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Margo downed her drink and said, 'Fasten your seat belts. It's going to be a bumpy night,' and I knew the mood had shifted dramatically.

grounded_facts: A gathering at Margo's home on a snowy night, hosted in anticipation of a larger celebration, where personal tensions and power dynamics surface among guests from the theater world.
memories.memory_text: I remember being at Margo's home on a snowy night, part of a gathering where tensions surfaced among the theater crowd, and I stayed quiet while things unfolded around me.

grounded_facts: Addison formally introduces himself to Eve, escorts her away from Margo, and positions himself as her mentor or ally.
memories.memory_text: I remember Addison introducing himself to me and linking his arm with mine, gently guiding me away from Margo while speaking about my passion for the theater.

grounded_facts: Addison tells Margo not to worry about Eve, implying he now has responsibility for her, undermining Margo's authority.
memories.memory_text: I heard Addison tell Margo not to worry about me, saying I was in safe hands, as he led me away and I smiled at her uncertainly.

grounded_facts: Margo locates the bicarbonate of soda in the cupboard and provides it to Max.
memories.memory_text: I saw Margo find the bicarbonate of soda in the cupboard and give it to Max, who then mixed it with water to settle his indigestion.

grounded_facts: Under Margo's insistence, Max promises to give Eve Harrington a job in his office.
Margo asks Max to give Eve a job in his office as a favor.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Margo asked Max to give me a job in his office, and after she insisted, he promised to do it.

grounded_facts: Margo proposes to help Max by reading with Miss Caswell for her audition.
memories.memory_text: I heard Margo offer to help Max by reading with Miss Caswell for her audition, saying she’d be a great help around the office and could take on tasks to free up his time.

grounded_facts: Margo reveals she is forty years old, marking a moment of personal vulnerability and self-awareness.
memories.memory_text: I remember when Margo said out loud that she was forty years old—she really emphasized it, like it was hard for her to admit.

grounded_facts: Lloyd suggests Margo's distress about age is actually about a fight with Bill.
memories.memory_text: I heard Lloyd suggest that Margo's upset about her age wasn't really about age at all, but about another fight she'd had with Bill.

grounded_facts: Despite her reservations about age, Margo decides to accept the role of Cora in Lloyd's play.
memories.memory_text: I saw Margo decide to accept the role of Cora, even though she had doubts about being too old, and she told Lloyd she would play the part.

grounded_facts: Eve speaks about the emotional reward of being loved by audiences nightly.
memories.memory_text: I remember speaking about how it feels to know that every night, different hundreds of people love me — their smiles, their shining eyes — and how I belong when I've pleased them and they want me. I said anything is worth that.

grounded_facts: A private moment in the pantry after a party, where key personal and professional decisions are made.
memories.memory_text: I remember the quiet moment in the pantry after the party, when Margo and Lloyd left the room and I became aware of their return, scrambling to my feet as they approached.

grounded_facts: The audition for Miss Caswell's role has already concluded by the time Margo arrives.
memories.memory_text: I was told the audition is over; it was called for 2:30 and now it's nearly four.

grounded_facts: Addison informs Margo that Eve Harrington has been appointed as her understudy, replacing the pregnant previous candidate.
memories.memory_text: I was told that I had been appointed as Margo's understudy, replacing the previous candidate who was pregnant.

grounded_facts: Margo presses Addison to reveal who read with Miss Caswell, showing growing concern and suspicion.
memories.memory_text: I saw Margo press Addison for answers about who read with Miss Caswell, and I could feel her growing suspicion.

grounded_facts: A scheduled theatrical audition originally set for 2:30 PM at the Curran Theater, where Eve Harrington delivered a standout performance.
memories.memory_text: I delivered my performance at the 2:30 audition at the Curran Theater, and Addison spoke of me as if I were destined for greatness, comparing me to legendary actresses.

grounded_facts: Addison passionately describes Eve's audition as a revelation, implicitly contrasting it with Margo's style.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Addison described my audition as a revelation, comparing me to legendary performers like Jeanne Eagels and saying I'd be among them.

grounded_facts: Addison describes Eve's reading as a transcendent performance that deeply impressed him and Lloyd.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Addison said my reading wasn't just a reading but a brilliant, vivid performance—something made of music and fire—that deeply impressed him and Lloyd.

grounded_facts: Margo sarcastically references a promise Max made, implying he broke it by hiring Eve.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Margo made a sarcastic comment about Max breaking a promise by hiring me, though I didn't hear it myself.

grounded_facts: Margo arrives late to the theater after the audition has concluded, unaware of Eve's new role.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Margo arrives late to the theater after the audition has concluded, unaware of Eve's new role.

grounded_facts: Eve claims she could not have performed if Margo had been present, subtly undermining Margo's presence.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Eve claims she could not have performed if Margo had been present, subtly undermining Margo's presence.

grounded_facts: An audition was held for the role, featuring Eve and Miss Caswell, which concluded before Margo arrived.
memories.memory_text: I remember that An audition was held for the role, featuring Eve and Miss Caswell, which concluded before Margo arrived.

grounded_facts: Margo accuses Lloyd of being overly impressed by Eve's performance, interpreting it as a personal attack.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Margo confronted Lloyd, and I realized she felt personally attacked by his praise for my performance — I could see how she interpreted his comments about the freshness of my reading as a slight against her.

grounded_facts: Margo threatens to leave the production, prompting Max to warn of legal consequences under her contract.
memories.memory_text: I saw Margo threaten to leave the production, and then Max warned her about breaking the contract, which made everything feel so tense.

grounded_facts: Lloyd blames Margo for turning a misunderstanding into a dramatic confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I heard Lloyd tell Margo that she turned a simple situation into a dramatic scene, saying she was playing a childish game and that she needed to remember she hadn't written the concerto herself.

grounded_facts: After the confrontation, both Lloyd and Max leave the theater, signaling a breakdown in professional relationships.
memories.memory_text: After the argument, I watched both Lloyd and Max walk out of the theater, and I knew things between them had fallen apart.

grounded_facts: Margo discovers that Eve has been appointed as her understudy without her knowledge.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Margo discovers that Eve has been appointed as her understudy without her knowledge.

grounded_facts: Bill physically restrains Margo and declares his love, attempting to ground her emotionally.
Bill physically restrains Margo to stop her from continuing her outburst, asserting emotional control.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill grab Margo and hold her down on the bed, stopping her from storming off, and then he told her he loves her, that she's beautiful and intelligent and a great actress, and that she has every reason to be happy.

grounded_facts: Bill asks Margo if marrying him would be enough to resolve her doubts, framing it as a final attempt to save the relationship.
memories.memory_text: I overheard Bill ask Margo if marrying him would be enough to resolve her doubts, framing it as his final attempt to save their relationship.

grounded_facts: Bill challenges Margo to reveal the real reason behind her behavior, accusing her of knowing but refusing to admit her true feelings.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bill challenge Margo to reveal the real reason behind her behavior, accusing her of knowing but refusing to admit her true feelings.

grounded_facts: As Bill leaves, Margo calls out and asks if he is going to find Eve, reigniting the jealousy that fueled the conflict.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Margo called out to Bill as he left, asking if he was going to find me, reigniting her jealousy.

grounded_facts: Bill declares that his attempt to reconcile is his last, and he leaves Margo after she fails to respond to his plea for honesty and change.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Bill declare that this was his last attempt to reconcile, and when Margo didn't respond, he left her for good.

grounded_facts: Lloyd praises Eve's talent and potential as an actress while speaking to Karen, implicitly criticizing Margo.
Lloyd shifts tone and speaks admiringly of Eve, contrasting her talent and potential with Margo's ego and resistance to change.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Lloyd praised me as a born actress—sensitive, vibrant, and full of potential—while talking to Karen, and that he contrasted my talent with Margo's ego.

grounded_facts: Lloyd returns home angry after a confrontation with Margo, criticizing her unprofessionalism and emotional outbursts during the audition.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Lloyd came home angry after clashing with Margo, feeling she was unprofessional and too self-absorbed to grow, though he didn't say it directly to me.

grounded_facts: Karen informs Lloyd that they are planning a weekend trip to the country with Bill and Margo.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Karen that they were planning a weekend trip to the country with Bill and Margo.

grounded_facts: After internal deliberation, Karen resolves that her idea is both harmless and beneficial, and initiates contact with Eve Harrington by phone.
memories.memory_text: I told myself that my idea wasn't just harmless—it would do the most good for all, and Margo would even enjoy it as a joke, though I wouldn't tell her right away, so I made the call to Eve Harrington to set things in motion.

grounded_facts: Karen places a phone call to Eve Harrington, marking the beginning of direct engagement.
memories.memory_text: I picked up the phone and asked to speak with Eve Harrington, marking the first time I directly reached out to her about my plan.

grounded_facts: A theatrical performance featuring Eve as the lead, following Margo's absence, attended by Addison and other press representatives.
memories.memory_text: I performed as the lead at the Curran Theater in place of Margo, and Addison was there with other press representatives to see me.

grounded_facts: Addison attended Eve's performance at the Curran Theater, which received enthusiastic applause from the remaining audience.
memories.memory_text: Addison attended my performance at the Curran Theater, and I heard the audience give me enthusiastic applause.

grounded_facts: Eve called Addison to invite him to attend her performance at the theater.
memories.memory_text: I called Addison that afternoon to invite him to attend my performance at the theater.

grounded_facts: Eve reveals her romantic feelings for Bill, implying that her success is tied to him and meant for him, but Bill rejects her advances.
memories.memory_text: I asked Bill if he was proud of me, and I told him my success was for him, hoping he’d see how I truly felt—like I did it all for us.

grounded_facts: Bill deflects Eve's confession of love by stating he is in love with Margo, causing Eve emotional pain.
memories.memory_text: I felt shattered when Bill told me he was in love with Margo—he said it so casually, like my feelings didn’t matter at all.

grounded_facts: A private moment in Margo's dressing room following Eve's successful understudy performance, where emotional and professional turning points occur.
memories.memory_text: I was in Margo's dressing room after my performance, a moment that felt like a turning point for me, where everything—my emotions, my future—seemed to hang in the balance.

grounded_facts: After Bill leaves, Eve violently slashes Margo's wig with scissors, symbolizing rage and frustration.
memories.memory_text: After Bill left, I glared at the door, tore the wig from my head, and threw it on the dressing table—I saw the scissors and in a sharp, vicious motion, I slashed the wig, feeling a rush of rage and frustration.

grounded_facts: Addison advises Eve to abandon excessive humility and embrace self-promotion, offering his column as a platform.
Addison offers to write about Eve in his column and suggests she embrace self-promotion, positioning himself as a powerful ally.
memories.memory_text: Addison told me I should stop being so humble and start promoting myself, and he offered to write about me in his column, positioning himself as someone who could guide my career.

grounded_facts: Eve agrees to have supper with Addison and implicitly accepts his role as a gatekeeper to fame, shifting her trajectory.
memories.memory_text: I agreed to have supper with Addison, and I think that night might open doors for me, though I’m not sure yet what it really means.

grounded_facts: Eve tells Addison to 'take charge,' signaling her willingness to be guided by him in both personal and professional matters.
memories.memory_text: I told Addison to 'take charge,' because I wanted him to lead the way, both in how we spent the evening and in shaping my future.

grounded_facts: Addison publicly affirms Eve's performance as 'magnificent,' reinforcing his support and influence.
memories.memory_text: I heard Addison say I was magnificent, and I felt his words carry weight in the room.

grounded_facts: Karen is surprised to learn that Addison was present at Eve's play the previous night, which she did not expect.
memories.memory_text: I was surprised when Karen asked if Addison had been at my play last night—he was there, and I didn’t expect him to show up.

grounded_facts: A planned lunch gathering involving Karen, Margo, Addison, and Eve, with an implied social and professional context.
memories.memory_text: I remember we were all gathered for lunch—Karen, Margo, Addison, and me—and it felt like something important was shifting between us.

grounded_facts: Addison asserts that Eve has no intention of going to Hollywood, reinforcing his control over her career decisions.
memories.memory_text: I was told at lunch that I have no intention of going to Hollywood, as if it were already decided, reinforcing that Addison is the one shaping my career path.

grounded_facts: Karen reads Addison's newspaper column titled 'Things I Promised Not To Tell' and becomes horrified, then abruptly leaves.
memories.memory_text: I saw Karen read Addison's column titled 'Things I Promised Not To Tell' and become horrified before she dropped the paper and rushed out.

grounded_facts: Lloyd informs Karen that Eve visited him and tried to explain her actions, but became emotional and couldn't finish.
memories.memory_text: I remember Lloyd telling Karen that I came to see him, tried to explain what happened, but got too emotional and couldn’t finish.

grounded_facts: Eve visited Lloyd before Karen arrived, during which she attempted to explain her interview and apologized indirectly, mentioning the play 'Footsteps on the Ceiling'.
memories.memory_text: I visited Lloyd before Karen arrived, and I tried to explain my interview and apologize indirectly, mentioning the play 'Footsteps on the Ceiling'—though I couldn’t bring myself to face Margo directly.

grounded_facts: Karen angrily opposes Lloyd's idea of casting Eve as Cora, accusing him of moral weakness and betrayal of Margo.
Karen strongly rejects the idea of Eve playing Cora, interpreting it as a betrayal of Margo and a sign of moral decay.
memories.memory_text: I heard Karen angrily reject the idea of me playing Cora, shouting that I was a contemptible little worm and that casting me would be a betrayal of Margo and a sign of moral weakness.

grounded_facts: Margo and Bill invite Lloyd and Karen to meet them at the Cub Room after the theater for wine, signaling a return to camaraderie.
memories.memory_text: I overheard Lloyd mention that Margo and Bill invited him and Karen to meet them at the Cub Room after the theater for wine, which seemed like a sign that their friendship was mending.

grounded_facts: After a phone call, Lloyd informs Karen that Margo and Bill want to meet them at the Cub Room after the theater.
memories.memory_text: I overheard Lloyd telling Karen that Margo and Bill wanted us to meet them at the Cub Room after the theater for a bottle of wine.

grounded_facts: After the argument, Lloyd clarifies that he did not promise Eve the role and cited Karen's opposition as a key reason.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Lloyd that he didn't promise me the role and mentioned Karen's opposition as a key reason, saying he wouldn't make a change without her approval.

grounded_facts: Lloyd reveals he has considered casting Eve Harrington in the lead role of 'Footsteps on the Ceiling', inspired during Eve's visit where she discussed the play.
memories.memory_text: I learned from Lloyd that he’s considering casting me as the lead in 'Footsteps on the Ceiling,' an idea he got while we were talking, though he mentioned there are practical difficulties and needs Karen’s approval.

grounded_facts: Eve Harrington sends a discreet note to Karen Richards, requesting an urgent meeting in the Ladies' Room during the celebration.
memories.memory_text: I sent a note to Karen during the celebration, asking her to meet me urgently in the Ladies' Room because I needed to speak with her right away.

grounded_facts: Margo and Bill reveal they will obtain a marriage license the next day at City Hall, initiating formal wedding proceedings.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Margo and Bill are getting their marriage license the next day at City Hall, starting their wedding plans.

grounded_facts: Margo notices Addison DeWitt seated nearby with signs that Eve had been with him, revealing their connection.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Addison DeWitt sitting near the entrance, and I could tell I had just been there with him—my crumpled napkin and wine glass were still at the table.

grounded_facts: As Karen passes his table, Addison rises and greets her warmly, but she ignores him.
memories.memory_text: I saw Addison rise and greet Karen warmly when she passed his table, but she ignored him completely and walked right past.

grounded_facts: Karen expresses limited sympathy and offers vague assistance, indicating a fragile reconnection.
memories.memory_text: I remember Karen offering me vague help, saying 'if there's anything I can do,' but her tone was guarded and her smile grim; she made it clear she wouldn't believe me easily, and I could feel how fragile our reconnection was.

grounded_facts: Eve attempts to regain Karen's trust by portraying herself as a victim of Addison's manipulation.
memories.memory_text: I tried to regain Karen's trust by confessing how Addison deWitt manipulated me, comparing his influence to an anesthetic that made me speak his words instead of my own, and I reached for her hand to make my plea feel more sincere.

grounded_facts: Eve explicitly demands that Karen tell Lloyd she should play Cora, framing it as the most important thing Karen can do.
memories.memory_text: I told Karen that getting Lloyd to cast me as Cora was the most important thing she could do for me, and I made it clear that the part was meant for me.

grounded_facts: Eve establishes a quid pro quo: her silence about Karen and Margo's incident in exchange for Karen recommending her for the role of Cora.
memories.memory_text: I made it clear to Karen that if I played Cora, Addison would stay silent about what happened between her and Margo — a simple exchange of favors, and I was happy to finally do something for her.

grounded_facts: Eve admits to Karen that her actions were influenced by Addison deWitt, acknowledging her own responsibility and disgrace.
memories.memory_text: I admitted to Karen that my actions were influenced by Addison deWitt and that the responsibility and disgrace were mine, using this confession to manipulate her into believing I was taking accountability while actually setting up a quid pro quo for the role of Cora.

grounded_facts: Eve threatens to expose Karen's complicity in covering up Margo's missed performance, leveraging Addison's knowledge to force Karen into supporting her for the role of Cora.
Eve reveals she knows Karen helped her cover Margo's absence and warns that Addison could expose the truth.
memories.memory_text: I reminded Karen that I know she helped cover up Margo's missed performance, and I let her know that Addison could expose everything if I don't get the role — but if I do play Cora, I’ll keep him silent.

grounded_facts: A private, emotionally charged conversation between Eve and Karen in the outer room of the Stork Club ladies' room.
memories.memory_text: I had a private, emotionally charged conversation with Karen in the outer room of the Stork Club ladies' room, where I confessed my actions, admitted my disgrace, and ultimately pressured her to support me for the role of Cora by leveraging Addison's silence.

grounded_facts: Eve reveals she spoke to Lloyd about playing the role of Cora and that Lloyd is interested, while Karen does not mention Margo's expected casting.
memories.memory_text: I told Karen that I had spoken to Lloyd about playing Cora, and that he was interested, making it clear I’m a serious contender for the role.

grounded_facts: Addison suggests Eve keeps things from him, hurting Eve's feelings and triggering a declaration of trust and reliance.
memories.memory_text: I felt hurt when Addison suggested I keep things from him, and I told him it wasn't funny—I don't like being accused like that. Still, I meant what I said about relying on him more than anyone else.

grounded_facts: A celebratory late-night gathering at the Cub Room where the group, including Margo and Bill on their wedding night, celebrates with champagne and conversation.
memories.memory_text: I was there at the Cub Room when the group celebrated late into the night with champagne, and even though Margo mocked me, I stayed and took it in.

grounded_facts: As Eve and Addison leave, Margo derides Eve as 'Eve evil, Little Miss Evil', reasserting dominance through theatrical scorn.
memories.memory_text: As Addison and I were leaving, I heard Margo call me 'Eve evil, Little Miss Evil'—her voice dripping with scorn—and I knew she was reasserting her dominance through mockery.

grounded_facts: Margo publicly declares she forgives Eve, linking her happiness to the group's unity, which she attributes to Eve's actions.
memories.memory_text: I heard Margo say she forgives me, and that our being together like this is my doing—she linked her happiness to the group's unity and said it was because of me.

grounded_facts: Margo shares her vision of domestic life and marriage with Karen, referencing shared memories.
memories.memory_text: Margo told Karen about wanting a real home and a man to come home to, and she asked if Karen remembered—like they had some shared past I wasn't part of.

grounded_facts: Margo declares she no longer wants to play 'Cora', citing her new married life and personal fulfillment as reasons.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Margo said she didn't want to play 'Cora'—she just stood up and declared it, like that was the end of it.

grounded_facts: After Margo rejects the role of Cora, Karen bursts into uncontrollable laughter, masking complex emotions.
memories.memory_text: After Margo rejected the role, I saw Karen suddenly burst into hysterical laughter—I couldn't tell if she was upset, relieved, or completely losing control.

grounded_facts: A rehearsal of the play where Eve performs a scene and conflicts arise between Bill and Lloyd over staging decisions.
memories.memory_text: I was performing my scene on stage, delivering my lines while moving upstage and turning to face the young man, which made him turn his back to the audience, and then Bill stopped everything to tell me I was supposed to stay downstage.

grounded_facts: Lloyd publicly claims responsibility for Eve's blocking decision to shield her from criticism.
Lloyd intervenes during rehearsal to justify Eve's blocking change, asserting his influence over the staging despite Bill's authority as director.
memories.memory_text: I saw Lloyd stand up and say that he was the one who told me to make the blocking change, taking the blame off me and defending my choice in front of everyone.

grounded_facts: Bill tells Lloyd to stick to writing and stop directing, leading to a public fight.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bill tell Lloyd to stick to writing and let him handle the directing, and it turned into a public argument right there during rehearsal.

grounded_facts: After a confrontation with Lloyd, Bill storms offstage, abandoning the rehearsal momentarily.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill come down to the footlights and argue with Lloyd, then throw his script into the auditorium before storming off with his coat.

grounded_facts: Eve retrieves Bill and persuades him to continue the rehearsal despite the conflict.
memories.memory_text: I went after Bill, pulled him back, and got him to pick up the rehearsal again even though he didn’t look at Lloyd.

grounded_facts: From the stage, Eve whispers to Lloyd, calming him after the conflict with Bill.
memories.memory_text: I whispered to Lloyd from the stage to calm him down, and I saw him smile and sit back down with Max.

grounded_facts: Eve is set to leave for New Haven, presumably for her first major theater performance, causing emotional strain.
memories.memory_text: I'm about to leave for New Haven tomorrow for my first major theater performance, and the pressure is making me feel completely overwhelmed.

grounded_facts: Addison uses military metaphor to frame Eve's upcoming performance as a conquest of immortality, offering encouragement.
memories.memory_text: I remember Addison telling me that I would win my beachhead on the shores of Immortality, as if my performance were a battle to conquer lasting fame.

grounded_facts: Eve expresses her certainty and excitement about the upcoming play's opening night, indicating a shift in her emotional state from anticipated anxiety to eager anticipation.
memories.memory_text: I told Addison how strange it felt—I thought I’d be panicked and want to run away before the premiere, but instead, I found myself completely eager for tonight to come and go.

grounded_facts: An out-of-town opening of a new play by Lloyd Richards, presented by Max Fabian, scheduled to take place at the Shubert Theater in New Haven that evening.
memories.memory_text: I remember seeing the marquee near the Taft Hotel and realizing it was the Shubert Theater where Lloyd Richards' new play, produced by Max Fabian, was opening that night.

grounded_facts: In response to Addison's suggestion of wealth, Eve asserts that her ambition is not for gold or diamonds but for stardom.
When questioned by Addison about the nature of her aspirations, Eve declares that her path forward is paved with stars, symbolizing her personal ambition and identity.
memories.memory_text: When Addison asked what my path was paved with, I told him it was stars—not gold or diamonds—because stardom is what I truly want.

grounded_facts: Addison refers to Eve as a 'killer', then quickly corrects it to 'champion', claiming confusion with boxing terms.
memories.memory_text: I remember Addison calling me a 'killer' as we walked to my door, then correcting himself to 'champion' when I asked why he said that — claiming he mixed up boxing terms.

grounded_facts: Eve calls out to stop Addison and invites him into her room for a private conversation.
Eve calls Addison back and invites him into her room, indicating she has something to tell him.
memories.memory_text: I called out to Addison as he was leaving and invited him into my room because I had something to tell him.

grounded_facts: An informal post-show event hosted by Eve and Lloyd for the theater company and associates.
memories.memory_text: I invited Addison to the post-show event Lloyd and I are hosting for the theater company tonight.

grounded_facts: Eve discloses to Addison that she and Lloyd Richards have decided to marry, believing their union will elevate her theatrical career.
memories.memory_text: I told Addison that Lloyd and I have decided to marry—he left Karen and came to me in the middle of the night—and I believe this will elevate my career because he’ll write great plays for me and make me a star.

grounded_facts: Addison declares that Eve will belong to him after the performance and will not marry anyone, establishing a coercive power dynamic.
memories.memory_text: I remember Addison telling me that after tonight, I would belong to him and that I wouldn't marry anyone, as if he had the power to decide my future.

grounded_facts: After Eve laughs at Addison's declaration of possession, he slaps her across the face and warns her never to laugh at him.
memories.memory_text: I laughed when he said I’d belong to him, and he slapped me across the face—hard—and told me to never laugh at him again, not at anyone, but never at him.

grounded_facts: Eve orders Addison to leave and, when he refuses, moves to call for help, asserting her space and autonomy.
memories.memory_text: I told Addison to get out, and when he wouldn't leave, I said I'd have him thrown out and then I went to call for help.

grounded_facts: A private, escalating confrontation between Addison and Eve following her announcement of an impending marriage.
memories.memory_text: After I told Addison about my marriage to Lloyd, he confronted me, towering over me and saying I’d belong to him from now on, mocking my past and dismissing my triumph, and I felt my confidence unravel as he exposed the truth I thought I’d buried.

grounded_facts: Addison reveals that Eve Harrington is actually Gertrude Slescynski, a woman who fled Milwaukee after a scandal involving her boss at a brewery.
memories.memory_text: I was told my name isn't Eve Harrington—that it's really Gertrude Slescynski, and that I fled Milwaukee after a scandal with my boss at a brewery, which his wife discovered when she had him followed by detectives.

grounded_facts: Addison confronts Eve with multiple truths disproving her fabricated identity and past, including the nonexistence of Eddie, her false marriage claim, and the fictional Shubert Theater in San Francisco.
memories.memory_text: I was confronted with the truth that Eddie never existed, I was never married, and I never performed in San Francisco—everything I said about those things was a lie.

grounded_facts: Addison directly accuses Eve of lying about performing in San Francisco, emphasizing its stupidity and ease of exposure.
memories.memory_text: I was told that my claim about performing in San Francisco was a stupid lie because there's no Shubert Theater there, and it was easy to expose.

grounded_facts: Addison declares their shared moral corruption and ambition, framing their bond as one of mutual contempt and insatiable drive, then demands Eve acknowledge she belongs to him.
memories.memory_text: I remember Addison telling me that we're both improbable people with a contempt for humanity, no ability to love, and insatiable ambition — and then demanding that I admit I belong to him.

grounded_facts: After emotional breakdown, Eve verbally acknowledges Addison's authority and ownership over her, accepting their twisted kinship.
memories.memory_text: I said 'Yes, Addison' twice — first when he asked if I was listening, and again when he demanded I acknowledge I belong to him — and in that moment, I accepted his authority over me.

grounded_facts: Despite Eve's declaration that she cannot perform, Addison insists she will give the performance of her life, effectively forcing her to continue.
When Eve says she cannot perform, Addison responds with a smile, asserting she will give the performance of her life, overriding her emotional state.
memories.memory_text: I told Addison I couldn't perform, that I wouldn't go on, but he just smiled and said I'd give the performance of my life, and I knew there was no way out.

grounded_facts: A private, intense confrontation in which Addison interrogates and emotionally breaks down Eve, exposing her lies and asserting control.
memories.memory_text: I remember being trapped in the room, breaking down and sobbing on the bed as Addison interrogated me, exposed my lies, and made me realize I belong to him completely—his words left me forlorn, and I eventually closed my eyes and fell asleep.

grounded_facts: A formal event honoring Eve with the Sarah Siddons Award, attended by theater figures and hosted by Max Fabian.
memories.memory_text: I was honored with the Sarah Siddons Award at a formal event attended by theater figures and hosted by Max Fabian.

grounded_facts: Eve is formally presented with the Sarah Siddons Award by the Aged Actor and delivers a public acceptance speech.
memories.memory_text: I was formally presented with the Sarah Siddons Award by the Aged Actor and delivered a public acceptance speech.

grounded_facts: Eve publicly thanks Max Fabian for giving her a chance as an unknown actress.
memories.memory_text: I publicly thanked Max Fabian for giving me a chance as an unknown actress, acknowledging his generosity and courage.

grounded_facts: Eve thanks Karen as her first friend in the theater.
memories.memory_text: I thanked Karen as my first friend in the theater, remembering her kindness and graciousness.

grounded_facts: Eve names Margo Channing as her idol and benefactor.
memories.memory_text: I named Margo Channing as my idol and benefactor, recalling how Karen first introduced me to her.

grounded_facts: Eve thanks Bill Sampson for his direction and patience.
memories.memory_text: I thanked Bill Sampson for his direction and patience, knowing he taught me well even when my talent fell short.

grounded_facts: Eve acknowledges Lloyd Richards for writing the play and believing in her.
memories.memory_text: I acknowledged Lloyd Richards for writing the play and believing in me, wondering how I could ever repay him.

grounded_facts: Eve reveals her upcoming move to Hollywood to make a film, while affirming her emotional commitment to theater.
memories.memory_text: I revealed I’m moving to Hollywood next week to make a film, but I made sure everyone knew my heart remains in the theater.

grounded_facts: Karen offers a brief, formal congratulation to Eve after the speech.
memories.memory_text: I remember Karen saying 'Congratulations, Eve' with a polite smile, and I thanked her, feeling grateful for her kindness even if it was brief.

grounded_facts: Margo delivers a sarcastic comment questioning Eve's emotional authenticity.
Margo responds to Eve's speech with a biting comment implying Eve lacks genuine emotion.
memories.memory_text: I heard Margo's sharp words after my speech—'nice speech, Eve'—and how she said I could put the award where my heart ought to be. I stood there, not knowing what to say, feeling the weight of her sarcasm questioning whether I truly felt anything at all.

grounded_facts: A high-class party hosted by Max Fabian in honor of Eve's award, planned to follow the ceremony.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Max Fabian planned a high-class party in my honor to follow the ceremony.

grounded_facts: Eve hands her Sarah Siddons Award to Addison, symbolically rejecting its value or her connection to the celebration.
memories.memory_text: I handed my Sarah Siddons Award to Addison and told him to take it to the party instead of me, showing that I didn't see the celebration as mine.

grounded_facts: After the ceremony, Eve decides not to attend the celebratory party hosted by Max Fabian.
memories.memory_text: I decided not to go to Max's party after the ceremony because I was tired and wanted to go home; when Addison reminded me how much trouble Max went to, I told him the party was for the award, not for me.

grounded_facts: Eve does not say good night to Addison before entering the hotel, indicating a deliberate or tense social break.
memories.memory_text: I think I made a point of not saying goodnight to Addison when I got out of the cab — it felt like a break, though I'm not sure how he took it.

grounded_facts: Eve exits a taxi in front of a fashionable apartment hotel without saying goodnight to Addison and enters the building.
memories.memory_text: I got out of the taxi in front of the apartment hotel and went inside without saying goodnight to Addison.

grounded_facts: Eve exits the taxi without taking the award with her, indicating it is no longer in her possession.
memories.memory_text: I got out of the taxi and realized I didn't have the award with me.

grounded_facts: Eve arrives at her apartment from the elevator and enters her home.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at my apartment from the elevator and let myself in.

grounded_facts: Phoebe panics when Eve moves toward the phone and begs not to be arrested, claiming she didn't steal anything.
memories.memory_text: When I moved toward the phone, she panicked and begged me not to call the police, saying she didn't steal anything and I could search her.

grounded_facts: An unsanctioned visit by Phoebe, president of a high school Eve Harrington fan club, who sneaks into Eve's hotel apartment to observe her lifestyle for a report.
memories.memory_text: I was told she’s the president of a high school fan club and came to study my lifestyle for a report on me.

grounded_facts: Phoebe, a fan from an Eve Harrington fan club, is discovered asleep in Eve's hotel apartment after sneaking in by exploiting the maid's temporary absence.
memories.memory_text: I discovered a girl asleep in my apartment, and when she woke up, she explained she had sneaked in while the maid was away to observe how I live.

grounded_facts: Phoebe tells Eve that a taxi driver returned the award, concealing Addison's visit and her own interaction with him.
